0-2-annual-chance-flood: Sometimes called a 500-year flood: a flood with a 0.2% chance of happening in any year. FEMA maps it as the shaded part of zone X.
1-annual-chance-flood: A flood with a 1% chance of being equalled or exceeded in any year (the base flood, sometimes called a 100-year flood). It is not once in 100 years: over 30 years the chance of at least one is 1 − 0.99^30 ≈ 26%.
USGS Water Science School, The 100-year flood
12-month-inflation: The percent change of a price index from the same month a year before: the usual way to state inflation. A 12-month rate of 3% means that prices are, on average, 3% higher than a year earlier, not that they rise 3% every month.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index: Frequently asked questions
303-d-list-impaired-waters: The list each state or territory submits under section 303(d) of the Clean Water Act of waters that do not meet water quality standards. EPA publishes the assessments in ATTAINS; the observatory measures the area that drains to or lies in a listed water.
US EPA, Overview of identifying and restoring impaired waters under Section 303(d)
3dep: The US Geological Survey's program that maps the height of the bare ground across the United States and its territories, mostly from lidar. Its 1/3 arc-second model gives a height about every 10 m.
400-m-rule: The observatory counts a place or census block as near transit when a stop lies within 400 m (about a quarter mile, roughly a 5-minute walk). Some measures use the straight-line distance and others the walking distance along mapped roads; each measure says which.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: The 400 m walking rule
501-c-3: The section of the US Internal Revenue Code for organizations exempt from federal income tax because they are organized and operated for charitable, religious, educational, scientific or similar purposes; donations to them are generally deductible.
aadt: Annual average daily traffic: the vehicles that pass a point of a road in a year, both directions, divided by the days of the year (vehicles a day). It is an annual average, so it says nothing by itself about a given hour.
FHWA, HPMS Field Manual (data item AADT)
acs: A yearly US Census Bureau survey that asks a sample of households about income, housing, work and more; in Puerto Rico it is run as the Puerto Rico Community Survey (PRCS). The observatory uses its 5-year estimates, which pool five years of answers and come with margins of error at 90% confidence.
US Census Bureau, About the American Community Survey
active-fire-detection: A satellite pixel that held one or more fires or other heat sources when the satellite passed. NASA FIRMS gives the pixel's centre (about 375 m across for VIIRS), not the fire's exact place or size, so detections are counted, not drawn as burned areas.
NASA Earthdata, FIRMS frequently asked questions
acuaexpreso: A passenger ferry service whose routes and stops are in the ATI timetable feed.
affordability-ratio: The median home value divided by the largest 30-year loan that a household with the median income could carry under the study's method. Above 1.0, the typical home is out of reach.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Home ownership affordability ratio
age-adjusted-rate: A rate recomputed as if the area had the age mix of a standard population (direct standardization): the area's rate in each age group is weighted by the standard's share of people in that group. It removes the part of a difference between areas that comes only from their age mix.
National Center for Health Statistics (CDC), Health, United States: Age adjustment
airport-certificated-for-airline-service: An airport that holds an FAA certificate under 14 CFR Part 139, which an airport needs to serve scheduled airline flights with more than nine passenger seats. In Puerto Rico: San Juan, Aguadilla and Ponce.
alltheplaces: An open project that collects business and store locations from company websites. Overture includes some of its records, which carry the CC0 1.0 public-domain dedication.
ama: Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (Metropolitan Bus Authority)
The Metropolitan Bus Authority. Its buses are in the ATI timetable feed.
annual-average: The average of a year's monthly or quarterly values. The jobs data give annual averages.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, QCEW overview
any-mapped-stop: A stop, station or terminal from any source: a stop in a timetable feed, even one that has ended, or a stop that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap with no timetable. The observatory's earlier 'within 400 m of transit' figures count these stops. They show where stops are, not where service runs today.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: How the observatory describes a tourism place's access to transport (the access profile)
apa-chicago-and-bibtex: Three ways to write a reference. APA 7 and Chicago are styles for printed text. BibTeX is a plain-text format that reference managers read. The Cite button on each entry offers all three.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: How to cite the observatory and its sources
api: An application programming interface: a defined set of requests by which one program asks another system for data or services. The build uses the public APIs of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, USAspending, OpenFEMA and several map servers.
NIST Computer Security Resource Center, Glossary: application programming interface
ardl: A regression of a series on its own past values and on current and past values of another series. Here: Puerto Rico's monthly price change on its last month, US inflation this month and last month, and one term for each calendar month.
Hyndman, R. J. and Athanasopoulos, G., Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition (OTexts), section 10.6, Lagged predictors
ask-the-observatory-chat: The question box on the 2D map. It answers from the map's datasets by fixed rules and is not a language model.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Ask the observatory: what stays on your device
assistance-listing: The public description of a federal assistance program (grants, loans, insurance, benefits and other aid), published at SAM.gov. Each has a number of the form 96.002, formerly called the CFDA number (Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance), which USAspending uses to group awards by program.
ati: Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (Integrated Transport Authority)
The Puerto Rico government agency that publishes timetable data for Tren Urbano, the AMA buses and the AcuaExpreso ferries. The observatory reads its GTFS files.
attribute: A value stored with a shape on a map: a barrio's name, its land area, its count of places. A layer keeps its attributes in a table with one row for each shape and one column for each attribute.
QGIS, A Gentle Introduction to GIS, Vector attribute data
audit-finding: A problem the auditor must report in a single audit: a weak control over a federal program, a rule of the program that was not followed, costs that are questioned, or fraud. Each finding has a reference number and names the federal program it is about.
Code of Federal Regulations, 2 CFR 200.1 (definitions) and 200.516 (audit findings)
average-mean: The sum of the values divided by how many there are. The jobs data's average pay is total wages divided by average jobs.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Measures of location
backtest: Testing a forecasting method on the past: from many starting months, forecast using only the data known then, and compare with what happened. Also called time series cross-validation or an out-of-sample evaluation.
Hyndman, R. J. and Athanasopoulos, G., Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition (OTexts), section 5.10, Time series cross-validation
barrio: A sub-municipal district. The Census Bureau calls the 901 barrios of Puerto Rico in its 2020 boundaries county subdivisions. A barrio name alone can point to more than one municipality.
base-map: The reference map of streets, water, land cover and place names drawn under the data layers. Every map of the observatory opens on OpenStreetMap data drawn as OpenFreeMap vector tiles (OpenMapTiles schema): the 2D map and the WCRP maps in the light 'Positron' style, the 3D view in 'Liberty'. On the 2D map and the 3D view the viewer can switch to three other OpenFreeMap styles, to the aerial imagery, topographic or shaded relief map of the USGS National Map, or to no base map. When it cannot load, the data show over a plain background.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: 2D map: base map, side panel and map controls
base-year: The earlier year from which a change is measured. The default is 2014 on the map and 2012 on the Housing page; both can be changed.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Change since the base year
basic-financial-statements: A government's annual financial report under the Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) standards: government-wide and fund statements with their notes, examined by independent auditors. They use accounting bases that differ from the budget's, so their totals are not the budget's spent figures.
Puerto Rico Department of the Treasury (Hacienda), Commonwealth of Puerto Rico Basic Financial Statements, June 30, 2023
bead: Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment Program

A federal program run by NTIA that pays to connect places without good home internet. It calls a location served at 100/20 Mbps or more, underserved at 25/3 up to 100/20, and unserved below 25/3, counting only cable, fiber, copper and licensed fixed wireless with low latency.
NTIA, Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) Program, Notice of Funding Opportunity (2022), section I.C
best-track: The National Hurricane Center's final, checked record of a storm's path and strength, built after the season. HURDAT2 holds the best tracks.
binary-file-bin: A file stored as raw numbers rather than readable text, so it is compact and fast to read. roads.bin holds the road network (junctions and the road pieces between them) that the route planner follows.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Road network (routing graph)
bivariate-map: A map that colours each place by two datasets at once, with three classes of each, so there are nine colours.
Esri ArcGIS Pro documentation, Bivariate colors symbology
block-group: A part of a census tract, generally with 600 to 3,000 people, and the smallest area for which the Census Bureau publishes survey estimates (grupo de bloques in Spanish). Puerto Rico has 2,555 in the 2020 boundaries; their survey estimates have the widest margins of error.
bls: A US federal agency that publishes jobs, wages, unemployment and price data. The observatory uses its QCEW, LAUS and CPI-U series.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, About BLS
bounding-box: A rectangle given by its west, south, east and north limits. The build asks for places inside one box that covers all of Puerto Rico, including Vieques, Culebra and Mona.
bridge-in-poor-condition: A highway bridge whose lowest rating among deck, superstructure, substructure (or culvert) is 4 or below on the 0–9 scale of the National Bridge Inventory. Poor does not mean unsafe; such bridges need repair or closer inspection.
broadband-serviceable-location: A place where the FCC says a home or business is, or could be, connected to fixed internet: a house, an apartment building, a business or a public building. An apartment building can be one location with many units. The FCC keeps the list (the Fabric) and updates it twice a year.
FCC, Broadband Data Collection: data specifications for the public availability data
bts: A US federal agency that publishes the National Transportation Atlas Database. The observatory takes the list of airports from the Federal Aviation Administration through it.
buffer: The area within a set distance of a point, line or area, drawn around it on the map. A buffer of 800 m around a stop is everything within 800 m of it in a straight line, not along the roads. A ring buffer leaves out the part closest to the feature: from 800 m to 1.6 km, say.
QGIS User Guide, Vector geometry: Buffer
building-footprint: The outline of a building on the ground, drawn as a polygon. Most are traced from aerial or satellite images, so they follow the roof (a roofprint). Overture joins OpenStreetMap's footprints, which come first, with ones that Google and Microsoft drew by machine learning.
cadastre: The map and inventory of every real property, each a parcel with its own number. Puerto Rico's Catastro Digital, kept by CRIM and updated from legal documents, exists to value property for taxes; it is not a survey map or a design tool.
CRIM, Manual de Usuario para la Aplicación Web del Catastro Digital de Puerto Rico (2020), Qué es el Catastro Digital
calificacion: Spanish for zoning classification: the zoning districts that the Junta de Planificación sets. The observatory does not publish a zoning layer: the Junta's map service was not available when the 2026-10 snapshot was built.
Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico
capital-gain: The profit from selling an asset, such as stock, a business or real estate, for more than its tax basis (roughly what was paid for it). The Opportunity Zone incentive defers and reduces the federal tax on gains invested in a Qualified Opportunity Fund.
IRS, Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses
catchment-nhdplus: The small area of land that drains directly to one stretch of stream in the USGS stream network, before the water joins the next stretch. Chaining catchments downstream gives the land that drains to any point.
cdbg: HUD's yearly formula grant for housing, public works and services that mainly benefit people of low and moderate income. In Puerto Rico, HUD pays the larger municipios directly (entitlement grants) and pays the Puerto Rico Department of Housing for the other municipios (the CDBG state program). The disaster grants CDBG-DR and CDBG-MIT are separate appropriations.
24 CFR part 570, Community Development Block Grants, eCFR
cdbg-state-program: The part of CDBG that HUD pays to a state, which passes it on to the local governments that do not receive their own entitlement grant. In Puerto Rico it is run by the Puerto Rico Department of Housing (through the 2018 grant, by the Office of the Commissioner of Municipal Affairs) for the other municipios.
24 CFR 570.480, State CDBG program, Legal Information Institute (Cornell)
cdbg-dr: Community Development Block Grant, Disaster Recovery

HUD grant funds for long-term recovery after a declared disaster. Foundation for Puerto Rico runs the WCRP program, which the observatory maps, in collaboration with PRDOH, with CDBG-DR funds from HUD.
cdbg-mit: HUD grant funds, first allocated in 2019 to places hit by the disasters of 2015 to 2017, for projects that reduce the risk of future disasters. In Puerto Rico the Puerto Rico Department of Housing manages them with its CDBG-DR grants.
HUD, Allocations, Common Application, Waivers, and Alternative Requirements for CDBG Mitigation Grantees, 84 FR 45838 (30 August 2019), GovInfo
cdla: A family of licenses for sharing data. Much of Overture's places data is under the permissive 2.0 version, which allows reuse and sharing. Check the license text for its conditions.
census-block: The smallest geographic area for which the Census Bureau tabulates the decennial count, often a city block bounded by streets or other features. The observatory uses the 2020 blocks that had residents.
census-tract: A small area that the Census Bureau draws for statistics, usually with 1,200 to 8,000 residents (sector censal in Spanish). Puerto Rico has 981 in the 2020 boundaries. Tracts fit inside municipios but not inside barrios.
centroid: The geometric centre (centre of mass) of a polygon. The observatory puts each sized symbol at the area-weighted centroid of the municipality's largest polygon, so detached islands do not pull it into the sea.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Sized symbols (proportional circles)
chas: HUD's Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy data: special tabulations of the American Community Survey on housing problems and cost burden by household income. A household has a severe housing problem when it lacks complete kitchen or plumbing facilities, has more than 1.5 persons per room, or pays more than 50% of its income for housing; CHAS counts cost burden as more than 30% of income.
HUD User, Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) data
choropleth-map: A map that shades areas by a value, for example municipalities by their poverty rate.
Esri ArcGIS Pro documentation, Graduated colors symbology
chronic-absenteeism: Missing 15 or more school days in a year, for any reason, excused or not. It counts students, not days, so it shows how many children miss a large part of the year.
US Department of Education, Civil Rights Data Collection: chronic absenteeism
cip-code: The federal code for a field of study. Its first two digits name a broad family (51 health, 52 business, 13 education); the observatory groups degrees by those families.
class-break: A value that separates one colour class from the next on a shaded map.
Esri ArcGIS Pro documentation, Data classification methods
cms: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the federal agency that runs Medicare and Medicaid. Its Provider Data Catalog lists hospitals, dialysis facilities, nursing homes, home health agencies and hospices.
code-library: A collection of ready-made code that a page loads to do a common job, such as drawing a map (Leaflet, MapLibre), a 3D scene (deck.gl) or a chart (Chart.js), instead of writing that code itself.
MDN Web Docs, JavaScript frameworks and libraries
cofog: Classification of the Functions of Government

The United Nations' standard classification of government spending by purpose, in ten divisions such as general public services, health and education, with groups below them. It lets budgets with different agency structures be compared by function.
United Nations Statistics Division, Classification of the Functions of Government (COFOG)
colmado: A small neighbourhood grocery, the corner store of Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic. The observatory counts it as a food store but not as a supermarket.
Asociación de Academias de la Lengua Española, Diccionario de americanismos: colmado
community-development-entity: An organization that the CDFI Fund certifies to receive New Markets Tax Credit allocations and invest them in low-income communities. It must serve those communities and keep their residents on its governing or advisory board.
26 U.S.C. 45D(c), Qualified community development entity (Cornell LII)
community-resilience-estimates: Census Bureau estimates of how many residents have risk factors that make it harder to cope with a disaster, among ten: low income, living alone, crowding, communication barriers, no employed person in the household, disability, no health insurance, being 65 or older, no vehicle and no broadband. Residents with three or more factors are counted as high risk.
U.S. Census Bureau, Community Resilience Estimates
community-water-system: A public water system that serves the same people all year: at least 15 service connections or 25 year-round residents, under the Safe Drinking Water Act. In Puerto Rico they are PRASA's systems and the community-run (non-PRASA) systems.
US EPA, Information about public water systems
commuting-flow: The number of workers who live in one place and work in another, here from one municipio to another. The Census Bureau tabulates it from the American Community Survey every five years, with a margin of error for each pair.
compliance-review: The state of a published file's reviews in the observatory's data contract: open (personal data, a license or federal grant content still under review, with the reason), cleared on a date, license not stated (at least one source states no license: a file takes the most restrictive license class of its sources), or not required. Federal grant content needs Finance and Compliance review before external communication.
PR Data Observatory, Data management: Definitions (Compliance review)
composite-index: A single measure built by combining several indicators, each normalized to a common scale and weighted, so that one number summarizes a multidimensional concept. Its value depends on the choice of indicators, normalization and weights.
European Commission, Joint Research Centre, Competence Centre on Composite Indicators and Scoreboards
comunidades-especiales: The communities designated under Ley 1-2001 for the Comunidades Especiales program and delimited by the Junta de Planificación in 2006 (713 outlines). They are low-income communities with special needs as the law defined them.
Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico
confidence-level: The probability, under repeated sampling, that a confidence interval contains the true value. The American Community Survey publishes its margins of error at the 90% confidence level.
US Census Bureau, Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data (2020), chapter 7: Understanding error and determining statistical significance
confidence-score: Overture's own score, from 0 to 1, for how likely a listing is a real place. The observatory counts places at 0.50 or higher by default.
constant-dollars: Also called inflation-adjusted dollars: dollars restated to the prices of one year so that different years can be compared. The map restates dollars to the latest CPI year.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index
consumer-price-index: An index of the prices a household pays for a fixed basket of goods and services, compared with a base period set to 100. Its change over time is the most used measure of inflation. Puerto Rico's official index is published by the Department of Labor and Human Resources (DTRH); the US index by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Handbook of Methods: Consumer Price Index, concepts
content-hash: The SHA-256 digest (its first 16 hexadecimal digits) of a data file's JSON in canonical form (keys sorted, no spaces), without the build dates written inside it; a file that is not JSON is hashed as bytes. Two versions with the same hash hold the same data.
PR Data Observatory, Data management: Definitions (Last updated)
contour-line: A line on a map that joins points of the same height above sea level, at a fixed interval (every 10 m, say). Lines close together mean steep ground; far apart, gentle ground.
QGIS User Guide, GDAL raster extraction: Contour
controlled-estimate: A survey figure that the Census Bureau forces to match its own population or housing estimate, so it has no sampling error and no margin of error. The total population of the island and of 76 of the 78 municipios is controlled.
US Census Bureau, ACS design and methodology
cool-roof: A roof made to reflect more sunlight and absorb less heat than a standard roof. It stays cooler in the sun and keeps the building below it cooler.
U.S. EPA, Using Cool Roofs to Reduce Heat Islands
correlation-r: The Pearson correlation coefficient: a number from −1 to +1 that measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two datasets across places. It does not show that one causes the other. The workbench's Correlations view can also use Spearman's rank correlation.
cossec: Public Corporation for the Supervision and Insurance of Cooperatives of Puerto Rico

The Puerto Rico public corporation that supervises the cooperativas de ahorro y crédito (savings and credit cooperatives) and insures their members' shares and deposits. The FDIC does not insure them, so they are not in the FDIC's files.
cost-burden: A household is cost-burdened when it pays 30% or more of its income for housing (the ACS cut-off the observatory uses; HUD's CHAS uses more than 30% and more than 50%), and severely cost-burdened at 50% or more.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Cost-burdened renters (30%+ of income on rent)
cost-of-living-adjustment: The yearly increase of Social Security and Supplemental Security Income benefits, effective in December: the rise of the average CPI-W of July to September over the same months of the last year with an adjustment, rounded to a tenth of a percent; zero when prices did not rise.
US Social Security Administration, Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) information
counted-not-drawn: The observatory's privacy rule: a private home, a holiday rental, a listing named by a street address, or a sensitive site such as a treatment facility is counted in its municipio but gets no point on the map, and its name and address are in no published file.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Counted but not drawn: the reason
county-subdivision: The Census Bureau's name for the areas below a county. In Puerto Rico they are the barrios.
covered-employment: Jobs at employers that pay into unemployment insurance. It leaves out self-employed people, unpaid family workers, informal work and military personnel.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, QCEW overview
cpi-u: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers

A Bureau of Labor Statistics index of how prices of goods and services bought by urban households change. The observatory uses the US city average, which it holds for 2000 to the latest full year, to restate dollars of different years.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index
cpi-w: Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers

The BLS consumer price index for households whose income comes mainly from hourly wages or clerical jobs, about a third of the US population. Social Security sets its yearly cost-of-living adjustment from it.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Handbook of Methods: Consumer Price Index, overview
crdc: A survey the US Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights runs every two years in every public school: enrolment, absences, discipline, courses and staff.
US Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights, Civil Rights Data Collection
crim: Centro de Recaudación de Ingresos Municipales (Municipal Revenue Collection Center)

The Puerto Rico agency whose Catastro Digital holds parcel-level data. The observatory does not use its data, because the license text on its services restricts redistribution; the Tools tab only opens CRIM's own viewer at a point.
Centro de Recaudación de Ingresos Municipales (CRIM)
csv: Comma-separated values: a plain-text table with one record per line and fields separated by commas (IETF RFC 4180). It opens in Excel and other spreadsheet programs; the observatory's tables download as CSV in UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, so Excel keeps the accents.
IETF RFC 4180, Common Format for CSV Files
cuerda: Puerto Rico's traditional unit of land area, still used in deeds and land records: 3,930.395625 m², about 0.39 hectares or 0.97 acres.
Ley de Pesas y Medidas del Estado Libre Asociado de Puerto Rico (Ley Núm. 145 de 27 de junio de 1968, según enmendada), sección 3
current-timetable: A timetable feed whose end date has not passed on the date the figures were computed. A stop has a current timetable when its operator's feed is current in this sense. It shows that a schedule is published for that date, not that vehicles run on time or at all. A feed with no end date does not count.
cut-off-from-hospitals: With no open road from home to any hospital. FEMA counts transportation as a community lifeline: when it fails, people cannot reach care and help cannot reach them. The observatory estimates who would be cut off when flooded roads or bridges in poor condition close.
damage-category-fema: The type of work a FEMA Public Assistance project pays for: emergency work (A, debris removal; B, emergency protective measures), permanent work (C, roads and bridges; D, water control facilities; E, buildings and equipment; F, utilities; G, parks, recreational and other facilities) and Z, management costs.
FEMA, Process of Public Assistance Grants
data-file: A file the observatory publishes in its data/ folder (JSON, GeoJSON or binary .bin), built from the sources; the pages read it to draw maps and tables, and anyone can download it.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Published data files
dataset: A set of related values on one subject from one source, for example unemployment by municipio and year. One data file can hold many datasets (economy_series.json holds dozens), and the dictionary documents each one as an entry.
daytime-population: The people in an area on a working day: its residents, plus the workers who come in to work, minus the workers who leave to work elsewhere. The Census Bureau calls it the commuter-adjusted population. It counts workers only, not students, shoppers or visitors.
US Census Bureau, Calculating Commuter-Adjusted Population Estimates
dc-fast-charging: Electric vehicle charging with direct current at high power, which can add about 160 to 320 km of range in 20 minutes. It needs a special connector and is found mostly along main roads.
US DOE, Alternative Fuels Data Center: Developing Infrastructure to Charge Electric Vehicles
de-duplication: Folding listings that appear to be the same place into one. The observatory keeps the one with the highest confidence.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: How duplicate listings are folded
de-obligation: An agency's cancellation or reduction of money it had committed. It lowers the total, so a few yearly values in some federal award categories are negative.
US GAO, A Glossary of Terms Used in the Federal Budget Process (GAO-05-734SP)
decennial-census: The count of everyone in the United States every ten years. The observatory uses the 2010 and 2020 counts.
US Census Bureau, Decennial Census of Population and Housing
denominator: The number you divide by. In jobs per 1,000 residents, the denominator is the number of residents.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Per 1,000 residents
design-hour-volume: The traffic of a road in its 30th-busiest hour of the year, in vehicles an hour: the hour engineers design capacity for. In HPMS it is AADT x K factor / 100. It is higher than a typical weekday peak hour.
FHWA, HPMS Field Manual, chapter 4, item 26: K_Factor
dfirm: FEMA's digital flood maps. The observatory selects Puerto Rico's flood polygons by the map code that starts with 72.
disaster-declaration: A formal federal decision that a disaster qualifies for FEMA help. The observatory's FEMA series are filed by the year of the declaration, not the year the money was spent.
FEMA, How a disaster gets declared
dissolve: Merging several areas of a map, such as municipios or barrios, into one area. A figure for the new area is the sum of its parts for a count, and must be pooled from the parts' numerators and denominators for a rate.
QGIS User Guide, Vector geometry: Dissolve
diverging-scale: A colour scale that shows distance from a natural centre: one colour above it, another below it, and pale grey near it.
ColorBrewer 2.0 (Brewer, Penn State), color advice for maps
domain-in-the-dictionary: A subject area that classifies the data dictionary's entries, such as Housing or Infrastructure. Each entry is tagged with one or more domains (the first is its primary domain), subdomains nest under a parent domain (Infrastructure › Mobility and transit), and the count beside each domain is the number of entries tagged with it or with one of its subdomains.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Browse by topic
drainage-area: The area of land whose rain and streams flow to a given point of a river or reservoir, measured flat on the map. USGS publishes it for each of its gauges.
USGS Water Services, Site Service (drain_area_va: drainage area)
drought-classes: The US Drought Monitor's scale: D0 abnormally dry, D1 moderate drought, D2 severe, D3 extreme, D4 exceptional. Each class is set so that conditions as dry happen about 20-30% (D0), 10-20% (D1), 5-10% (D2), 2-5% (D3) or under 2% (D4) of the time.
e-rate: The federal Schools and Libraries Program of the Universal Service Fund, run by USAC, which discounts telecommunications and internet services for schools and libraries. The observatory's public libraries are those registered in it.
echo: EPA's Enforcement and Compliance History Online, the public database of permits, inspections and violations. The observatory takes from it the community water systems under the Safe Drinking Water Act.
US EPA, Enforcement and Compliance History Online (ECHO)
ecological-fallacy: The mistake of assuming that what is true of an area, on average, is true of each person who lives in it. A barrio with a high poverty rate also has residents who are not poor.
UCGIS GIS&T Body of Knowledge, Problems of Scale and Zoning (FC-07-026)
ecostress: ECOsystem Spaceborne Thermal Radiometer Experiment on Space Station

A NASA thermal infrared instrument on the International Space Station since 2018. It measures land surface temperature at about 70 m. Because the station's orbit is not tied to the sun, it passes each place at a different hour each time, night included, unlike Landsat, which always passes mid-morning.
eia-860m: Form EIA-860M, Monthly Update to the Annual Electric Generator Report

The US Energy Information Administration's monthly inventory of the electric generators at plants of 1 MW or more: each generator's nameplate capacity, technology and status, and its plant's location. Puerto Rico has its own sheets of operating, planned and retired generators. Rooftop solar is not in it: each system is under 1 MW.
US Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-860M (Monthly Update to the Annual Electric Generator Report)
employment-rate: Employed civilians as a share of all residents 16 and over. The base includes retirees, students and everyone else who is not in the labor force, so it is lower than the share of the labor force that has a job.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Glossary
ems: Emergency medical services: the system of ambulances and emergency medical personnel that gives care before and during transport to a hospital. The observatory maps fire and EMS stations from the USGS structures data.
NHTSA Office of EMS, What is EMS?
english-speaking-ability: The American Community Survey asks people who speak a language other than English at home how well they speak English: very well, well, not well or not at all. It is the person's own rating, not a test. People who answer below "very well" are counted as speaking English less than "very well".
US Census Bureau, About language use in the United States
entitlement-grant-cdbg: The CDBG money HUD pays each year straight to a large city or urban county by formula, without competing for it. In Puerto Rico, HUD made entitlement grants to 27 municipios for 2025.
24 CFR part 570, subpart D, Entitlement Grants, eCFR
epa: The US Environmental Protection Agency. The observatory uses its data on toxic releases (TRI), risk management plans (RMP), Superfund sites (NPL), impaired waters (ATTAINS), non-attainment areas (Green Book), landfills (LMOP) and water systems (ECHO).
equal-intervals: A way to set map classes by cutting the range from the lowest to the highest value into equal widths.
Esri ArcGIS Pro documentation, Data classification methods
equal-area-hexagon: A cell of a grid in which every hexagon covers the same ground area, so counts in different hexagons compare directly as densities. The observatory draws its hexagons on an equal-area map projection centred on Puerto Rico.
Snyder, J. P. (1987), Map Projections: A Working Manual, USGS Professional Paper 1395 (Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection)
ersv: Foundation for Puerto Rico's strategic plan for the east of the island. Its Eastern Region is a fixed set of 15 whole municipios: Canóvanas, Ceiba, Culebra, Fajardo, Humacao, Juncos, Las Piedras, Loíza, Luquillo, Maunabo, Naguabo, Río Grande, San Lorenzo, Vieques and Yabucoa. A regional figure is the sum of its municipios, or a pooled rate (the sum of the parts over the sum of the base), never an average of municipio rates.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Regions (groups of whole municipios)
establishment: One work site of an employer with employees, such as a single store or factory. A company with ten stores has ten establishments.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Glossary
estimate: A value computed from a sample or a model rather than from a count of everyone, and so subject to error. Survey figures, the annual population estimates (PEP) and the unemployment figures are estimates; decennial census counts are not.
US Census Bureau, Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data (2020), chapter 7: Understanding error and determining statistical significance
ev-charging: A point where electric vehicles can charge. The observatory maps the public stations in the US Department of Energy's list and, on another layer, the charging points volunteers added to OpenStreetMap.
US Department of Energy, Alternative Fuels Data Center: electric vehicle charging stations
evapotranspiration: All the ways water moves from the land to the air: evaporation from soil and water, and transpiration, the water plants release through their leaves. It takes heat from the surface, which is one way vegetation cools a place.
USGS Water Science School, Evapotranspiration and the Water Cycle
expected-annual-loss: FEMA's estimate of the average dollars lost each year to natural hazards: damage to buildings and crops, and lives valued in dollars by FEMA's rule. It multiplies what is exposed by how often each hazard strikes and how much damage it does, so it is higher where there is more to lose. A model estimate, not a record of losses.
FEMA, National Risk Index: Expected Annual Loss
expected-inflation: The average inflation that markets and forecasters anticipate over a horizon. The Cleveland Fed estimates it for 1 to 30 years from Treasury yields, inflation swaps and survey forecasts; the expectation over k years can be split into the expected rate of each single year.
Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, Inflation Expectations
expired-timetable: A timetable feed whose end date has passed. The observatory counts these stops in some figures and leaves them out of the 'current' ones.
exposure: How many residents, housing units or places lie inside a hazard (flood zone, sea level rise, high landslide susceptibility), inside protected land, or near transit. The observatory computes it from open layers by giving each census block to the area that holds its internal point; it is not a measure of damage.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: How exposure is counted (census blocks counted whole by their internal point)
express-route: A bus service that skips most or all stops on part of its path, so it runs faster between a few stations. ATI route 20 (Estación Bayamón to Terminal Campanilla) has two stops.
Transit Capacity and Quality of Service Manual, 3rd edition (TCRP Report 165)
faa: The US agency that keeps the list of airports. The observatory takes it as the official list and drops overlapping airport points from OpenStreetMap.
fars: NHTSA's census of every crash on a public road in which someone died within 30 days, coded from police reports and other records, with Puerto Rico in its own files.
fdic: The US federal agency that insures deposits in banks, up to a limit per depositor, and supervises many banks. Each June it asks every insured bank how much it holds in deposits at each of its offices (the Summary of Deposits).
federal-audit-clearinghouse: The federal government's public repository of single audits, run by the US General Services Administration (GSA) at fac.gov, which took it over from the Census Bureau. Each audit lists the federal money the entity spent, program by program.
federal-award-types: The observatory sorts federal awards into contracts, grants, direct payments, loans and other assistance. Contracts buy goods or services, grants fund a purpose, direct payments go to individuals, and loans are credit. For loans the observatory counts the estimated cost to the government, not the amount lent. Other covers insurance and other assistance.
federal-awards-expended: The federal money an entity used in its fiscal year, by the rules of the single audit: the money spent on a program's activities, plus the amount of a federal loan drawn or still owed where the rules count it. It is money spent, not money awarded or obligated.
eCFR, 2 CFR 200.502 Basis for determining Federal awards expended
federal-share: The part of a project's eligible cost that the federal government pays under a cost-sharing rule; the recipient or applicant pays the rest (the non-federal share). For FEMA Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation it is usually 75%, and can be raised, as it was for Puerto Rico after the 2017 hurricanes.
fema: The US agency for disaster response and recovery. It publishes flood hazard maps (the NFHL) and disaster aid data (OpenFEMA).
ffata: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act
The 2006 federal law that created USAspending.gov and requires the prime recipients of federal grants and contracts to report their first-tier subawards, usually those of $30,000 or more.
Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006, Public Law 109-282, GovInfo
fhwa: Federal Highway Administration: the agency of the US Department of Transportation that funds and sets standards for federal-aid highways and publishes national road data such as HPMS and the National Bridge Inventory.
FHWA, Office of Highway Policy Information
field: A variable the records of a data file carry: a column of a table, a GeoJSON property, a series variable or its margin of error; a cell that holds a list counts as one field. A field is counted when at least one record holds a value in it.
PR Data Observatory, Data management: Definitions (Field)
fips: Standard numeric codes for places. Puerto Rico's state code is 72, and a municipality code adds three digits, for example 72127 for San Juan.
US Census Bureau, ANSI and FIPS codes
first-published: The date a data file first reached the published site, in Puerto Rico time; it never moves (the release date, dcterms:issued, of the W3C DCAT vocabulary).
PR Data Observatory, Data management: Definitions (First published)
fiscal-year: A 12-month budget year. The US federal fiscal year runs from October 1 to September 30 and is named for the year it ends: FY2025 is October 2024 to September 2025.
US GAO, A Glossary of Terms Used in the Federal Budget Process (GAO-05-734SP)
fitted-line: The ordinary least-squares line: the straight line that minimises the sum of the squared vertical distances to the points of a scatter plot. The vertical distance from each point to it is that point's residual.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Linear least squares regression
five-year-window: The five years of survey responses pooled into one American Community Survey 5-year estimate, for example 2020–2024. The observatory labels each window by its last year.
US Census Bureau, Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data (handbooks)
fixed-wireless: Home internet sent by radio from a tower to an antenna on the building. Licensed fixed wireless uses radio channels the provider has rights to; unlicensed uses shared channels that can be crowded, so BEAD does not count it as reliable.
FCC, Broadband Data Collection: data specifications for the public availability data
flood-zone: A FEMA map category for an area's flood hazard, written as a letter code such as A, AE, AH, AO, A99, V, VE, X or D. Zones A and V, with their variants, are the Special Flood Hazard Area; zone D marks an area where a flood hazard is possible but FEMA has not studied it.
floodway: The regulatory floodway: the channel of a river and the adjacent land that must be kept free of encroachment so the 1% annual chance flood can pass without raising the water surface by more than a designated height.
food-access: How easily people can reach a store that sells healthy, affordable food, usually measured by the distance to the nearest supermarket. The USDA's Food Access Research Atlas measures it for the states and leaves Puerto Rico out; the observatory measures road distance itself.
USDA Economic Research Service, Food Access Research Atlas: documentation
fpr: The nonprofit that develops the PR Data Observatory as a tool for public use and benefit. It also wrote the 2023 housing study that the observatory draws on.
fqhc: A Federally Qualified Health Center: a health center funded by HRSA's Health Center Program to serve a medically underserved area or population; a look-alike meets the same requirements without the grant. The observatory counts the sites in HRSA's Service Delivery and Look-Alike Sites file, so its counts include look-alikes.
HRSA Bureau of Primary Health Care, What is a health center?
free-flow: Traffic moving at the speed the road allows, with no congestion slowing it. A free-flow drive time is a lower bound: real trips at rush hour take longer.
FHWA, Traffic Data Applications: what traffic data are (travel time relative to free-flow conditions)
frequent-stop: In the observatory, a stop with a current timetable and 20 or more weekday calls. 20 is a threshold chosen for the observatory, not a standard. 'Frequent service' in the app means a frequent stop within 400 m of the place.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: How the observatory describes a tourism place's access to transport (the access profile)
fta: The US agency that runs the National Transit Database, which lists transit agencies that report to it.
fte: A way to count practitioners by the time they work: one FTE is one practitioner working full time, so two half-time practitioners are one FTE. HRSA applies its own rules to the hours it counts, so a practitioner can count as a fraction of an FTE or as none.
HRSA Data Warehouse, Health workforce shortage areas (HPSA and MUA/P)
functional-class: The role a road plays in the network: freeways and arterials carry long trips at higher speeds, collectors gather traffic from neighbourhoods, local streets give access to homes. Arterials and major collectors are classes 1 to 5.
FHWA, Highway Functional Classification Concepts, Criteria and Procedures (2023)
gap-status: A code from 1 to 4 in the protected-areas database (PAD-US) for how an area is managed for biodiversity. 1 is permanent protection from conversion of natural land cover, with a management plan to keep a natural state; 4 has no known mandate for protection.
USGS, PAD-US Standard Tables (designation types and GAP Status Code descriptions)
gazetteer: A list of place names with their coordinates. The observatory's place search uses one built from OpenStreetMap names and Census boundaries.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Place-name index
geoid: The Census Bureau's code for an area. A municipality's GEOID has five digits: 72 for Puerto Rico and three digits for the municipality. A barrio's GEOID is longer and starts with it.
US Census Bureau, Understanding geographic identifiers (GEOIDs)
geojson: A standard format (IETF RFC 7946) for encoding geometries (points, lines and polygons) with their attributes in JSON, in WGS 84 longitude and latitude. Most of the observatory's map layers, such as flood.geojson, are GeoJSON files.
geometric-mean: The n-th root of the product of n values. A price index that averages price changes this way assumes that buyers shift a little toward items whose prices rise less; it gives a slightly lower rate than an arithmetic mean of the same prices.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Handbook of Methods: Consumer Price Index, calculation
gerd: gross domestic expenditure on research and development

Gross domestic expenditure on R&D: all spending on research and experimental development performed in the economy in a year, by businesses, government, higher education and private non-profits, whatever the source of funds; usually expressed as a percentage of GDP (Frascati Manual definition).
UNESCO Institute for Statistics, Glossary (UIS Data Browser)
gigawatt-hour-gwh: A unit of energy: one million kilowatt-hours (kWh), or 1,000 megawatt-hours. Puerto Rico produces about 18,000 GWh of electricity a year.
gii: The Global Innovation Index, published every year by WIPO (with Cornell University and INSEAD until 2020): about 80 indicators grouped in 7 pillars, normalized to 0-100 and averaged into an input and an output sub-index and an overall score for each economy covered. Puerto Rico is not among them; FPR's 2021 profile placed Puerto Rico's values among the GII 2020 economies.
gini-index: A measure of income inequality from 0 (every household has the same income) to 1 (one household has all the income).
gis: A computer system that stores, analyzes and displays information tied to a place on the earth. It keeps a map's shapes together with the facts about each one, so it can answer questions such as what is near a place or what falls inside an area.
U.S. Geological Survey, What is a geographic information system (GIS)?
github: A website where software projects are shared. This site is hosted there, the nightly transit refresh runs there, and the wish list of the Ask the observatory chat can open a data request there.
government-effectiveness: A WGI dimension: perceptions of the quality of public services, of the civil service and its independence from political pressure, and of the quality of policy formulation and implementation and the credibility of the government's commitment to it. A standardized estimate centred on 0.
World Bank, Worldwide Governance Indicators: documentation (2026 update)
gps: Global Positioning System: the US satellite navigation system that gives position and time. The observatory's "vehicles now" views replay timetables; they are not GPS tracking.
gross-enrolment-ratio: Enrolment in a level of education, whatever the students' age, as a percentage of the population of the official age for that level (for tertiary, the five years after secondary school). It can exceed 100% because of late entrants, repeaters and older students.
UNESCO Institute for Statistics, Glossary (UIS Data Browser)
gross-rent: The monthly rent plus the cost of utilities that the renter pays.
gtfs: General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS Schedule): the standard set of text files in which transit agencies publish their timetables, with stops, routes, trips and stop times. The observatory reads GTFS feeds from ATI and from municipal systems.
gtfs-rt: The companion standard for live vehicle positions and delays. In the 2026-10 snapshot ATI lists its feed as in development ('en desarrollo'), so the observatory has no live bus data.
h3: A grid that covers the Earth with hexagons of fixed sizes, each with its own id. At resolution 8 a hexagon covers about 0.74 km², about 460 m across. The FCC places every broadband serviceable location in one, so places can be compared on cells of the same size instead of on boundaries of different sizes.
H3 documentation: Tables of cell statistics across resolutions
hazard-mitigation-assistance-fema: FEMA's grant programs for projects and plans that reduce the loss of life and property from future disasters: the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (after a disaster declaration), Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities, Flood Mitigation Assistance and the earlier Pre-Disaster Mitigation program. FEMA generally pays up to 75% of eligible costs.
head-start: A federal program of the US Department of Health and Human Services that funds local agencies (municipalities, consortia and nonprofits) to give children from birth to age 5 in families with low income early learning, health and family services at no cost.
Administration for Children and Families, Office of Head Start: Head Start Services
headway: The scheduled time between consecutive departures on a route at a stop, in minutes. The observatory gives the average for four parts of the day, from the published timetable.
hexagon-grid: A tiling of the map into equal-area hexagons (2, 10 or 50 km² each) used to count points. Because every cell has the same area, the count in a cell is also a density.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Tourism places counted in hexagons and by municipality, under your filters
hhi: A measure of concentration. The observatory uses it for jobs: the sum of each sector's squared share of jobs, times 10,000. A higher number means fewer sectors hold most of the jobs.
US Department of Justice, Herfindahl-Hirschman Index
hhs: US Department of Health and Human Services
The US Department of Health and Human Services, the federal department that includes HRSA, SAMHSA and CMS. The observatory places hospitals at HHS's geocoded addresses.
high-volume-intersection: In the Route analysis, a signalised junction or roundabout (OpenStreetMap) where the busiest road within 30 m carries an estimated 2,000 or more vehicles an hour in the design hour (HPMS 2024: AADT x K factor, the 30th-busiest hour of the year; the class median K where the road has none). An estimate of volume, not a measure of delay.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: High-volume intersections on the path
hls: A NASA product that processes Landsat 8 and 9 and Sentinel-2 images the same way, at 30 m, so they can be used as one series. Together the satellites see a place about every 2 to 3 days, against 16 for Landsat alone.
NASA Goddard, Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) project
hmda: A US law that requires most lenders to report every application for a home loan they receive: where the home is, the amount, the purpose and whether the loan was made or denied. The CFPB and the FFIEC publish the reports each year.
Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Mortgage data (HMDA)
hmgp: The FEMA grant opened by a presidential major disaster declaration that funds long-term mitigation projects and plans across the declared state or territory; its size is a percentage of the disaster's other federal assistance.
horn-s-method: The usual way to compute slope from an elevation grid: the east-west and north-south change in height at a cell are taken from its eight neighbours, the nearest ones counting twice. GDAL, QGIS and ArcGIS use it by default.
hot-spot: An area where high values or many events are closer together than chance alone would put them, by a statistical test. A place that simply has many events is a concentration; it is a hot spot only if the test says so.
Getis and Ord (1992), The Analysis of Spatial Association by Use of Distance Statistics, Geographical Analysis 24(3)
household: All the people who live in one housing unit. The number of households equals the number of occupied housing units.
housing-unit: A house, apartment, mobile home or room meant as separate living quarters, occupied or empty.
hpms: Highway Performance Monitoring System: the national road inventory the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) keeps from yearly state reports, with traffic (AADT, K factor), lanes and condition for each reported section of state and federal-aid roads. Most local streets are not in it.
hpsa: A federal designation, made by HRSA, for an area, a group of people or a facility that has too few primary care, dental or mental health practitioners for the people it serves.
hrsa: The agency of the US Department of Health and Human Services that funds community health centers and designates health professional shortage areas. The observatory reads four of its public data files.
http-header: A line of information a browser sends with each request to a server, and the server with its answer: for example the browser's name and version (user agent), the languages it prefers and the address of the page that made the request (referrer).
hud: US Department of Housing and Urban Development

The US Department of Housing and Urban Development, the federal housing agency. Its CDBG-DR funds pay for the WCRP program, which Foundation for Puerto Rico runs in collaboration with PRDOH; the observatory also uses HUD's CHAS data and its list of public housing developments.
hurdat2: The National Hurricane Center's record of Atlantic storms since 1851 with each storm's track and wind speed. The observatory uses it to draw storms that came near Puerto Rico.
NOAA National Hurricane Center, Data archive (HURDAT2)
iata-and-icao-codes: Codes that identify airports. IATA codes have three letters and ICAO codes have four.
IATA, Airline and location code search
ihp: FEMA's program of help for households after a disaster. The observatory's housing assistance series count the households approved for it and the dollars approved.
inbound-mobility: Students from abroad enrolled in the economy's tertiary education, as a percentage of all its tertiary students (the UIS inbound mobility rate).
UNESCO Institute for Statistics, Glossary (UIS Data Browser)
index-puerto-rico-100: A value shown as a percent of the Puerto Rico value, so the island equals 100. A municipality at 120 is 20% above the island.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Index (Puerto Rico = 100)
indicative-position: On the GII page: the place Puerto Rico's updated value would take among the GII 2026 economies with data for the same indicator, written X/N, where X is 1 plus the number of economies with a strictly better value and N counts those economies plus Puerto Rico. Calculated by FPR; it is not an official WIPO rank, and no pillar or overall score follows from it.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Indicative position among the GII 2026 economies
individual-assistance-fema: FEMA help for households after a disaster. The observatory shows the households approved for housing assistance and the dollars approved.
inspector: The first workbench view. It shows every visible layer's value for one place, beside Puerto Rico as a whole, with a small trend line whose caption gives the number of years it covers.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Trend line in the inspector and the Trend chart
integration-point: A place where stops of two different operators are within 250 m of each other, a natural spot to align timetables, fares and signs.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Integration points
internal-point: A point that the Census Bureau places inside each area (INTPTLAT, INTPTLON), at or near its geographic centre and always within the area. The observatory assigns a census block to a hazard or district by this point.
interquartile-range: The difference between the 75th and the 25th percentile (Q3 − Q1): the spread of the middle half of the values, which extreme values do not affect. On the GII page, a change smaller than 5% of it is shown as no meaningful change (≈).
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Measures of scale
ip-address: A number that identifies a device on the internet. A website or server that a page contacts can see it.
NIST Computer Security Resource Center, Glossary: Internet Protocol
ipeds: The US Department of Education's yearly survey of every college and university that takes federal student aid: who enrols, who graduates and in what.
iri: How rough a road's surface is, measured by a vehicle driving it, in inches of vertical movement per mile. FHWA counts more than 170 as poor and less than 95 as good.
irs: The US Internal Revenue Service. It recognizes tax-exempt organizations and publishes their list (the Exempt Organizations Business Master File), from which the observatory counts nonprofits by municipio.
iso-8601: The international standard for writing dates and times, for example 2026-10-02T02:31:31+00:00. The observatory writes its build time this way.
ISO, ISO 8601 date and time format
javascript: The programming language that web pages run in your browser. The observatory's maps, charts and calculations run in JavaScript on your own device, so the pages need it switched on.
jenks: The method behind natural breaks: it chooses class limits at the biggest gaps in the data. See Natural breaks.
Esri ArcGIS Pro documentation, Data classification methods
job-accessibility: How many jobs can be reached from a place within a set travel time, such as 30 minutes by car: a count of the opportunities within reach, not the distance to the nearest one.
University of Minnesota Accessibility Observatory, Access Across America: Methodology 2024
jp: The Puerto Rico government planning agency. It published the 2015 land use plan that the observatory draws.
Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico
json: JavaScript Object Notation, a standard plain-text format for structured data (IETF RFC 8259): objects of name and value pairs, and lists. Many of the observatory's data files are JSON, for example municipalities.json; GeoJSON is JSON for geometries.
IETF RFC 8259, The JSON Data Interchange Format
k-factor: HPMS data item 26 (K_FACTOR): the design-hour volume, the 30th-busiest hour of traffic in the year, as a percentage of the road's AADT. AADT x K / 100 is that design-hour volume in vehicles an hour, not a typical weekday peak. HPMS requires it only on Sample Panel sections and says statewide or system-wide values shall not be used.
FHWA, HPMS Field Manual, chapter 4, item 26: K_Factor
karst: Land on limestone that water dissolves, with sinkholes, caves and streams that run underground. About a fifth of Puerto Rico, mostly in the north, is karst, so water there does not follow the surface streams alone.
Giusti, E. V. (1978), Hydrogeology of the karst of Puerto Rico, USGS Professional Paper 1012
kilovolt-kv: A unit of electric voltage: 1,000 volts. The higher a line's voltage, the more power it can carry over a long distance with smaller losses: Puerto Rico's backbone runs at 230 kV, homes are served at 120 and 240 volts.
kurtosis: A measure of how heavy the tails of a distribution are relative to a normal distribution (whose kurtosis is 3). High kurtosis means more extreme values; the GII uses a threshold of 3.5 together with skewness to flag outliers.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Measures of skewness and kurtosis
labor-force: Residents 16 and over who are working or looking for work.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Glossary
labor-force-participation-rate: The labor force (people employed or unemployed and looking for work) as a percent of the population of the same age, usually 16 and over. The observatory's survey rates count the Armed Forces in the labor force, as Census Bureau table S2301 does; the rest of the population is not in the labor force (students, retired people, people caring for their home).
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Glossary
land-cover: What covers the ground's surface, as seen from above: forest, grass, crops, water, wetlands, bare ground or buildings and pavement. It differs from land use, which is what people use the land for (housing, farming, conservation).
NOAA National Ocean Service, What is the difference between land cover and land use?
land-surface-temperature: The radiative skin temperature of the ground, roofs, pavement or canopy, in kelvin or degrees Celsius, derived from a satellite's thermal infrared bands and the surface's emissivity. It is not the air temperature 2 m above the ground: on a sunny afternoon a dark roof can be 20 °C or more hotter than the air.
landsat: The joint NASA and USGS series of Earth-observing satellites, imaging the land since 1972. Landsat 8 and 9 carry a thermal infrared sensor (TIRS, about 100 m) from which USGS derives land surface temperature; each passes over Puerto Rico every 16 days, about 10:30 local time, 8 days apart.
landslide-susceptibility: The relative likelihood that the ground at a location fails in a landslide triggered by intense rainfall, mapped by USGS for Puerto Rico in classes from low to extremely high. It describes the terrain, not the chance of a landslide in a given year.
USGS Open-File Report 2020-1022, Map depicting susceptibility to landslides triggered by intense rainfall, Puerto Rico (Hughes and Schulz, 2020)
last-updated: The last date the content of a data file changed, that is, the date its content hash first differed from the one before (the modification date, dcterms:modified, of W3C DCAT). A rebuild that writes the same data on another day does not change it.
PR Data Observatory, Data management: Definitions (Last updated)
laus: A Bureau of Labor Statistics program that estimates unemployment for counties and municipalities. It uses models, so figures for small areas are smoothed.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Local Area Unemployment Statistics
layer: One set of data drawn on the map, such as flood zones or transit stops, that can be switched on or off and stacked with others.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: 2D map: base map, side panel and map controls
legend: The key to a map's symbols and colours. It says what each one stands for and, on a shaded map, which values each colour covers.
QGIS Documentation, A Gentle Introduction to GIS: Map Production
level-2-charging: Electric vehicle charging with alternating current at 240 volts, which adds about 16 to 32 km of range an hour: a full charge takes several hours. It is the most common public charger.
US DOE, Alternative Fuels Data Center: Developing Infrastructure to Charge Electric Vehicles
licence: The terms under which a source lets others use, share and change its data. The observatory records each source's licence, and a dictionary entry carries the strictest licence among its sources; licence text is what each source states, not legal advice.
Open Knowledge Foundation, The Open Definition 2.1
lidar: A remote sensing method that measures distance with pulses of laser light, usually from an aircraft, and records millions of 3D points of the ground, buildings and vegetation. From the ground returns a bare-earth elevation model is made; USGS 3DEP publishes Puerto Rico's at 1 m.
NOAA National Ocean Service, What is lidar?
life-table: A table of the chance of dying at each age and, from it, how many of a group of people would still be alive at each later age. It lets a count of people at one date be carried forward to the next.
United Nations, World Population Prospects 2024: Methodology report (life tables)
lihtc: A federal tax credit for building or rehabilitating rental housing for lower-income households; in Puerto Rico the Housing Finance Authority allocates it. The map's tax credit housing layer shows the projects in HUD's database, and Table 10 of the 2023 housing study lists projects that also received disaster recovery money.
HUD User, National Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) Database
lmop: EPA's Landfill Methane Outreach Program, whose database lists municipal solid waste landfills, open or closed, with their location.
US EPA, Landfill Methane Outreach Program (LMOP)
loan-subsidy-cost: The government's estimate of what a federal loan or loan guarantee will cost it over its life, after repayments and expected defaults. It is not the amount lent, and it can be negative when estimates are revised. The observatory's federal loans series uses it.
US GAO, A Glossary of Terms Used in the Federal Budget Process (GAO-05-734SP)
local-mean-sea-level: The average height of the sea at a place, worked out from hourly tide readings over many years, used as the zero from which heights there are measured. A reservoir's level in metres above local mean sea level is the height of its water surface above that zero, not the depth of the water.
NOAA Tides and Currents, Datum options: Mean Sea Level (MSL), the arithmetic mean of hourly heights over the National Tidal Datum Epoch
location-quotient: A sector's share of a municipality's jobs divided by its share of Puerto Rico's jobs. A value of 1 means the same concentration as the island.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Location quotients explained
log-transformation-gii: For a skewed indicator with more than five outliers, the GII replaces each value x by ln[(max − 1)(x − min)/(max − min) + 1] before the min-max normalization, which compresses the long upper tail and keeps the order of the values. In the GII 2026 it applies to 9 indicators, such as domestic market scale.
WIPO, Global Innovation Index 2026, Appendix I: Conceptual and measurement framework
long-run-pass-through: In a model of one price index on another, how much of a lasting one-point change in the second ends up in the first, after all the lags have worked through. A pass-through of 1 means one for one.
Hyndman, R. J. and Athanasopoulos, G., Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition (OTexts), section 10.6, Lagged predictors
look-alike: A health center that meets the requirements of the federal Health Center Program but does not receive its grant. HRSA lists its sites together with those of funded health centers.
HRSA Bureau of Primary Health Care, What is a health center?
low-latency: A connection whose round-trip delay is 100 milliseconds or less, as the FCC defines it. Video calls and games need it; geostationary satellite internet does not have it.
FCC, Broadband Data Collection: data specifications for the public availability data
low-income-community-opportunity-zones: For the 2027 Opportunity Zones, a census tract whose median family income is at most 70% of its area's, or whose poverty rate is 20% or more with a median family income at most 125% of its area's; the area is the metropolitan area the tract is in, or the state outside one. Treasury measured both with the 2020-2024 American Community Survey.
US Treasury, Office of Tax Analysis: Eligibility criteria for 2027 Qualified Opportunity Zones (October 2026)
linea-pas: Línea de Primera Ayuda Sicosocial (psychosocial first aid line) of ASSMCA

The crisis intervention line of ASSMCA (Administración de Servicios de Salud Mental y Contra la Adicción), Puerto Rico's mental health and addiction services agency: 1-800-981-0023, listed with 988, answered 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, by a multidisciplinary team of mental health professionals, with a chat at lineapas.assmca.pr.gov and sign-language video relay (VRS) at 787-615-4112. It offers crisis counselling and emotional support, a preliminary psychosocial screening, coordination of psychiatric and psychological evaluation and of drug and alcohol rehabilitation, and referrals.
ASSMCA, Línea PAS (Programa Integrado de Intervención en Crisis)
machine-learning: Computer methods that learn patterns from examples instead of following rules written by a person. Google and Microsoft used it to trace building outlines from satellite images; such outlines are fast to make for a whole country but can include sheds or miss buildings under trees.
NIST Computer Security Resource Center, Glossary: machine learning (NIST SP 800-55 Vol. 1)
map-projection: A way of flattening the round Earth onto a map. Each projection keeps some things true and stretches others. To measure distances and areas in metres, use a projection made for the place, such as NAD83 / Puerto Rico & Virgin Is. (EPSG:32161).
QGIS, A Gentle Introduction to GIS, Coordinate reference systems
map-scale: How much smaller the map is than the ground. On a map at 1:25,000, one centimetre stands for 250 metres. The scale bar on a map shows a real distance at the current zoom.
QGIS Documentation, A Gentle Introduction to GIS: Map Production
map-style: A JSON document, in the MapLibre Style Specification, that says which vector tiles to read and how to draw each layer (colours, line widths, labels, the zoom levels at which each appears), with the addresses of its fonts and icons. The same tiles can be drawn in several styles, such as OpenFreeMap's Liberty and Positron. A style can also point to raster tiles, as the observatory's USGS base maps do.
map-tile: One square piece of a web map at one zoom level and place. A map is drawn from many tiles side by side, and the browser asks a server only for the tiles of the area on the screen, so the requests show which area is being viewed.
mb-and-gb: Units of file size. In the observatory, 1 MB = 1,048,576 bytes (2^20) and 1 GB = 1,024 MB: the binary multiples that NIST names mebibyte (MiB) and gibibyte (GiB).
mbps: How much data a connection moves each second, in millions of bits. Speeds are written download/upload: 100/20 Mbps means 100 Mbps to the home and 20 Mbps from it.
FCC, Broadband Data Collection: data specifications for the public availability data
median: The middle value of the sorted data (the 50th percentile): half of the values are lower and half are higher. A median income is less affected than a mean by a few very high incomes.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Measures of location
median-family-income: The income in the past 12 months of the family in the middle of an area's families: half have more and half less. A family is a household of two or more people related by birth, marriage or adoption; people living alone are left out, so it is higher than median household income.
US Census Bureau, American Community Survey and Puerto Rico Community Survey subject definitions: Income
medicare: The federal health insurance program for people 65 and older and for some younger people with disabilities or end-stage renal disease. The observatory uses CMS's monthly enrollment counts by municipio.
megawatt-hour-mwh: A unit of energy: one megawatt of power delivered for one hour, or 1,000 kilowatt-hours (kWh). For a battery, MW says how fast it can deliver power and MWh how much energy it can store.
meta-pr: Medición y Evaluación para la Transformación Académica de Puerto Rico
Puerto Rico's yearly standardized test in public schools: Spanish, math and English in grades 3 to 8 and 11, and science in 4, 8 and 11. Puerto Rico sets its own levels.
Instituto de Estadísticas de Puerto Rico, Proficiencia en las pruebas estandarizadas (META-PR)
min-max-normalization: Rescaling of an indicator to a fixed range, here 0 to 100: score = 100 × (x − min) / (max − min), with the smallest and largest value of the economies in the sample; for indicators where higher values are worse the scale is inverted, 100 × (max − x) / (max − min). It keeps the order of the values, so it does not change ranks.
WIPO, Global Innovation Index 2026, Appendix I: Conceptual and measurement framework
mipr: The Junta de Planificación's online map service, which holds the zoning districts (Calificación). The observatory publishes no zoning data from it.
Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico
modifiable-areal-unit-problem: The same data can give different maps and different statistics depending on the areas it is added up in: larger or smaller areas, or areas with other boundaries. A pattern seen by municipio may change or vanish by barrio.
UCGIS GIS&T Body of Knowledge, Problems of Scale and Zoning (FC-07-026)
moe: Margin of error: half the width of the confidence interval around a survey estimate, written with ±. The American Community Survey publishes it at the 90% confidence level: the interval estimate ± MOE contains the true value with 90% confidence.
US Census Bureau, Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data (2020), chapter 7: Understanding error and determining statistical significance
mua-p: A federal designation, made by HRSA, scored from four indicators: providers for each 1,000 people, infant deaths, poverty and the share of people aged 65 and over. The observatory does not use the file for Puerto Rico because its indicators are empty there.
HRSA Data Warehouse, Health workforce shortage areas (HPSA and MUA/P)
municipio: Spanish for municipality. Puerto Rico has 78 municipios, which the Census Bureau treats like counties. The observatory says municipality in English text.
naics: A code system for kinds of business. Two-digit codes name broad sectors, for example 72 for accommodation and food services, and longer codes name narrower groups such as 721 for accommodation.
US Census Bureau, North American Industry Classification System
nalcab: National Association for Latino Community Asset Builders
A national nonprofit that funded the 2023 housing study in part, through its Advancing Equitable Neighborhood Development program.
NALCAB, National Association for Latino Community Asset Builders
nameplate-capacity: The maximum rated output of a generator under the manufacturer's conditions, in megawatts (MW; 1 MW = 1,000 kW). It is installed capacity, not the electricity actually produced.
national-register-of-historic-places: The official federal list of buildings, sites, districts, structures and objects judged worthy of preservation, kept by the National Park Service. Listed private homes are counted by municipio but not drawn.
National Park Service, What is the National Register of Historic Places?
natural-breaks: A way to set map classes that finds the biggest gaps in the data, so values in a class are as alike as possible.
Esri ArcGIS Pro documentation, Data classification methods
ndvi: A measure of how green the land looks from a satellite: (near-infrared − red) / (near-infrared + red). Green leaves reflect near-infrared light and absorb red, so values near 0 mean rock, sand, pavement or roofs, about 0.2 to 0.5 sparse cover such as grass and shrubs, and about 0.6 to 0.9 dense vegetation such as forest. It ranges from −1 to +1; water is below 0.
USGS, NDVI, the Foundation for Remote Sensing Phenology
net-metering: An arrangement in which a customer with solar panels or another small generator is billed only for the electricity it takes from the grid minus what it sends to the grid. In Puerto Rico the utility registers each system; the observatory reports their number and capacity, never a customer.
net-migration: The people who moved into a place minus the people who moved out of it over a period. Negative means more left than arrived; it says nothing of how many moved each way.
United Nations, World Population Prospects 2024: Methodology report (definitions)
network-analysis: Measuring along a network of connected lines, such as roads, instead of in a straight line: the shortest way between two points, or everything that can be reached within a distance or a time.
new-markets-tax-credit: A federal tax credit for investments in businesses and real estate projects in low-income census tracts. The CDFI Fund (US Treasury) gives Community Development Entities the right to offer it; investors put money into a CDE, which lends or invests it in the tract, and the investors claim 39% of the investment over seven years.
CDFI Fund, New Markets Tax Credit Program
nfhl: FEMA's digital database of flood zone maps. The observatory draws its Puerto Rico polygons and tests each tourism place against them.
nhc: The US National Weather Service center, part of NOAA, that tracks and forecasts tropical storms. Its HURDAT2 database is the source of the observatory's storm tracks.
NOAA National Hurricane Center, About the NHC
nhsc: A federal program, run by HRSA, that places clinicians in shortage areas. HRSA's priority score ranks the shortage areas for it.
night-light-recovery: Reading how fast an area got back to normal after a disaster from satellite pictures of light at night: the light falls in a blackout and rises as power and activity return. It is a proxy, not a count of homes with power.
Román et al. (2019), Satellite-based assessment of electricity restoration efforts in Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria, PLOS ONE 14(6): e0218883
noaa: The US agency for weather, oceans and coasts. It supplies the sea level rise layers and the hurricane records the observatory uses.
nominal-dollars: Dollars of the year they were earned or spent, with no adjustment for inflation.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index
non-attainment-area: An area that EPA designates as not meeting a National Ambient Air Quality Standard for a pollutant, listed in the Green Book. In Puerto Rico: San Juan and Guayama-Salinas for sulfur dioxide (2010 standard) and Arecibo for lead (2008 standard).
