not-seasonally-adjusted: A series as measured, with the changes that repeat at the same time each year (such as school costs in August) left in. The 12-month rate compares the same month of two years, so it is not much affected by them.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Seasonal adjustment in the CPI
npdes-permit: The federal permit a facility needs to discharge wastewater into a river, a lake or the sea. It sets limits on what may be discharged and requires the facility to measure and report it. EPA issues these permits in Puerto Rico. An individual permit is written for one facility; a general permit covers many similar ones, such as construction sites.
npi: The ten-digit number every health care provider who bills in the United States must have. Its registry (NPPES) lists each provider's practice address and specialty.
CMS, National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES)
npl: The Superfund National Priorities List: EPA's list of the sites of known or threatened releases of hazardous substances that are the priority for long-term cleanup.
US EPA, Superfund National Priorities List (NPL)
nps: The US National Park Service, which keeps the National Register of Historic Places.
ntd: A Federal Transit Administration database of transit agencies. The observatory uses its list of Puerto Rico agencies as a checklist of systems that exist, whether or not they publish a timetable.
ntee-code: A code of the National Taxonomy of Exempt Entities that classifies a nonprofit by its main activity, for example arts, education or health. The IRS list carries it; an organization with no code or the unknown code is counted as unclassified.
Urban Institute, National Center for Charitable Statistics: IRS activity codes (NTEE)
nw-cm-sr: nanowatts per square centimetre per steradian

The unit of night-time light radiance (written nW·cm⁻²·sr⁻¹ by NASA): billionths of a watt (10⁻⁹ W) of light per square centimetre of ground per steradian, the SI unit of solid angle (the cone of directions the sensor looks through). It measures brightness, not the number of lights.
NASA LAADS DAAC, VNP46A3 product page (units of the radiance layers)
obligation: A federal agency's legal commitment to pay for an award. Obligated dollars are promised amounts, not necessarily money already paid.
US GAO, A Glossary of Terms Used in the Federal Budget Process (GAO-05-734SP)
odbl: The license for OpenStreetMap data. It asks users to credit OpenStreetMap contributors and keep derived databases open. Read the license for the full terms.
Open Data Commons, Open Database License (ODbL)
open-data: Data that anyone can freely access, use, change and share for any purpose, subject at most to conditions that keep its origin credited and its openness (Open Definition 2.1).
Open Knowledge Foundation, The Open Definition 2.1
openfema: FEMA's public data service. The observatory takes its housing assistance records and its Public Assistance project records, by municipality and disaster year.
openfreemap: A free public service that serves OpenStreetMap as vector tiles in the OpenMapTiles schema, with ready-made map styles, no key and no request limit, but no service guarantee. It is the observatory's tile provider for every map.
openmaptiles: An open schema for vector tiles made from OpenStreetMap: it fixes the tile layers (transportation, building, water, place, poi and others) and their fields. Its licence asks maps that use it to show '© OpenMapTiles'.
opportunity-zone: A low-income census tract that the US Treasury has designated, on a state's nomination, so that capital gains invested there through a Qualified Opportunity Fund get federal tax benefits (26 U.S.C. 1400Z-1). Since 2027, each designation lasts ten years and a state may have at most a quarter of its eligible tracts.
IRS Revenue Procedure 2026-14 (designation of 2027 Qualified Opportunity Zones)
orthoimagery: Aerial or satellite photographs corrected so that each point sits where it would on a map: the tilt of the camera and the relief of the ground are taken out, so distances and areas can be measured on them. The USGS National Map's orthoimages range from 15 cm (6 inches) to 1 m per pixel; at the scale of the whole island its base map shows coarser satellite mosaics instead.
USGS, The National Map: USGS Imagery Only base map service (service description)
osm: A free map of the world edited by volunteers, under the ODbL. The observatory uses it as the data of every base map (through OpenFreeMap), and for bus stops, taxi stands, EV charging points, públicos routes and the road network.
osm-element: OpenStreetMap element: node, way or relation

One object of the OpenStreetMap database: a node (one point, with latitude and longitude), a way (an ordered list of up to 2,000 nodes: a street, a river or the outline of an area) or a relation (an ordered group of nodes, ways and other relations, such as a bus route or a multipolygon). IDs are numbered separately for each type, so an element is named by its type and ID, as in its page openstreetmap.org/way/<ID>.
outlay: A payment the federal Treasury makes to settle an obligation, for example to a grant recipient. Outlays follow obligations, often over several years, so an award can be fully obligated and only partly paid out.
US GAO, A Glossary of Terms Used in the Federal Budget Process (GAO-05-734SP)
outlier: A value that lies far from the pattern of the other values, such as the value of a municipality that is far from those of the rest.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Detection of outliers
overlaid: A figure made by laying one published map layer on another and counting what falls inside: the schools inside a flood area, for example. Nothing is assumed or modelled. It tells where things are, not what will happen to them.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Public facilities in the 1% flood area
overlay: Laying one map layer over another to find where their shapes meet: which places fall inside a flood zone, how much of a barrio is protected land. The result is a count or a share, or a new layer cut along both sets of edges.
overture: An open map data project. Its places data are the source of the observatory's tourism places.
pad-us: Protected Areas Database of the United States
The US Geological Survey's national map of protected land and water. The observatory uses version 4.1 for Puerto Rico.
USGS Gap Analysis Project, PAD-US data overview
pan: Programa de Asistencia Nutricional (Nutrition Assistance Program)

Puerto Rico's food assistance for low-income households. It is paid from a fixed federal block grant, not through SNAP; Puerto Rico writes the program's rules and the US Department of Agriculture approves them each year.
US Department of Agriculture, Nutrition Assistance Program (NAP) block grants
pass-through-entity: An organization that receives a federal award and passes part of it to another organization (a subrecipient) to carry out part of the program, for example a Commonwealth agency that gives part of a federal grant to a municipio.
peak-hour: The hour of the day with the most traffic on a road (or the most riders on a transit line). The Route analysis counts the morning peak period as 6:00-9:00 and the afternoon peak as 16:00-19:00.
pedestrian-bridge: A bridge for people on foot over a road, river or rail line (in OpenStreetMap, a footway, path, steps or cycleway tagged bridge). The observatory joins the pieces of one bridge and counts it once.
pell-grant: A federal grant from the US Department of Education that helps undergraduate students with financial need pay for college; it does not have to be repaid. The money goes through the college or university the student attends.
eCFR, 34 CFR 690.1 Federal Pell Grant Program, scope and purpose
pep: The Census Bureau's program that estimates population each year between censuses. The observatory uses its July 1 estimates for municipalities.
US Census Bureau, Population and Housing Unit Estimates
per-1-000-residents: A count divided by the number of residents and multiplied by 1,000. It makes municipalities of different size comparable.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Per 1,000 residents
per-capita: Per person: a total divided by the number of residents. The map shows dollar totals per resident.
percent-change: How much a value grew or shrank compared with where it started: (new − old) ÷ old × 100. The observatory uses it for counts and dollars.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Change since the base year
percentage-point: The unit for the difference between two percentages, written 'pts' in the observatory. A rise from 20% to 25% is 5 percentage points, or 25% in relative terms.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Difference from Puerto Rico
percentile: The pth percentile is the value below which p% of the sorted values fall. A percentile rank goes the other way: it is the share of values below a given value, from 0 to 100, or from 0 to 1 as on the WCRP page. It says how a place ranks against the others, not by how much it differs.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Percentiles
period-of-performance: The time between a federal award's start date and its end date, during which the recipient may carry out the work and incur costs. After the end date the recipient has a set number of days to draw down what it is owed, and the agency then closes the award.
Code of Federal Regulations, 2 CFR 200.1 (definitions) and 200.344 (closeout)
pet: A thermal comfort index in °C: the air temperature of a standard indoor room (no wind, no sun) at which a person's body would reach the same heat balance as outdoors, given air temperature, humidity, wind and radiation. Higher PET means more heat stress; above about 41 °C is classed as extreme heat stress on the usual scale for temperate climates.
Höppe (1999), The physiological equivalent temperature, International Journal of Biometeorology 43:71-75
pillar-gii: One of the seven groups of indicators of the Global Innovation Index: five input pillars (institutions, human capital and research, infrastructure, market sophistication, business sophistication) and two output pillars (knowledge and technology outputs, creative outputs). A pillar's score is the weighted average of its sub-pillars.
Cornell University, INSEAD and WIPO, The Global Innovation Index 2020, Appendix III: Sources and definitions
pl-94-171: The Census Bureau's counts for small areas, released for drawing voting districts. The observatory uses its 2010 and 2020 housing counts, taken on census day.
US Census Bureau, Decennial census summary files (redistricting data, PL 94-171)
place-of-performance: Where the work of a federal award is done or its benefit goes, as the awarding agency reports it. Awards for statewide programs are often recorded in the capital.
placed-in-service: For a tax credit housing building, the date it is ready and available for tenants. The owner claims the credit for ten years from that year or the next, and HUD's LIHTC database records the year.
places-of-worship: Churches and other places of worship. The observatory maps them but leaves them out of its counts by default, because most are not tourism supply.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Which places the observatory counts (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship)
pmtiles: A single-file format for map tiles. A web page reads only the pieces of the file it needs, by asking the server for byte ranges, so a large map can be served from plain web hosting without a tile server.
png: An image file format that keeps every pixel exactly (lossless compression), so lines, labels and the colours of a map stay sharp. Any device, browser or office program opens it.
W3C, Portable Network Graphics (PNG) Specification (Third Edition)
point-in-polygon: A test of whether a point lies inside a shape. The build uses it to find the municipality, flood zone, protected area and land use class of each place.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: How points, stops and blocks are assigned to a municipality
polygon: A closed planar shape bounded by a ring of straight segments, with optional holes (a GeoJSON Polygon, RFC 7946). Municipios, barrios, flood zones and protected areas are polygons; a MultiPolygon is a set of them, such as a municipio with islands.
pooled-rate: The rate of a group of areas computed from their summed counts (the sum of the numerators over the sum of the denominators), not as an average of the areas' rates. Each area then weighs as much as its population; an unweighted average would give a small municipio the same weight as a large one.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Women in the labor force (Knowledge Area data)
pooled-values: Values from several years put into one list. With 'Same classes in every year' on, the observatory pools the values of all years before it sets the class limits.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Same classes in every year
posted-for-load: A bridge with a sign limiting the weight of the vehicles that may cross it, because its structure cannot safely carry the legal loads. FHWA codes it in item 41 of the National Bridge Inventory, with bridges that should be posted and bridges closed.
FHWA, Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (item 41)
poverty-level: The federal income cut-off below which a person is counted as in poverty. The observatory reports the share of people whose income in the past 12 months was below it.
US Census Bureau, How the Census Bureau measures poverty
ppp: Purchasing power parity: a conversion rate that equalizes what a currency buys across economies, so GDP in PPP dollars (international dollars) compares volumes of output rather than market exchange rates. Estimated by the World Bank's International Comparison Program.
prasa: Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority
The Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority (Autoridad de Acueductos y Alcantarillados, AAA), the public utility that runs most of the island's drinking water and sewer systems.
Autoridad de Acueductos y Alcantarillados (AAA, PRASA)
prcs: The Census Bureau's survey of households in Puerto Rico, run in the same way as the American Community Survey. Its 5-year estimates are the survey figures in the observatory.
US Census Bureau, Puerto Rico Community Survey
prdoh: The Puerto Rico Department of Housing (Departamento de la Vivienda), the government agency for housing. FPR runs the WCRP program in collaboration with it.
Departamento de la Vivienda de Puerto Rico
prediction-band: A range around a forecast meant to hold the actual value a stated share of the time. On the Inflation page the 80% band is the central path plus or minus 1.28 times the method's root mean square error in the backtest, and the 95% band 1.96 times.
Hyndman, R. J. and Athanasopoulos, G., Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition (OTexts), section 5.5, Distributional forecasts and prediction intervals
prime-working-age: Ages 25 to 54, when most people have finished school and have not yet retired. A participation rate for these ages compares areas with less influence from how many young people study or how many older people are retired.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Labor force participation, women 25 to 54
principal-and-interest: The two parts of a loan payment: paying back the amount borrowed and paying the lender for the loan.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Affordability method: settings and rounding rules for the municipality fields
proclamation-boundary-proc: A protected-area designation that outlines a whole island or refuge. The observatory draws it but does not count a place inside one as protected.
USGS, PAD-US Standard Tables (designation types and GAP Status Code descriptions)
proficient-test-level: Scoring at or above the level a state sets as meeting the grade's standard. Each state and Puerto Rico sets its own test and its own line, so shares are not comparable across them.
US Department of Education, EDFacts assessment data documentation
project-closeout: FEMA's final step for a Public Assistance project: the recipient documents the completed work and its final costs, and FEMA reconciles them with what it obligated. A project can be physically finished long before it is closed out.
FEMA, Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG), closeout
project-based-rental-assistance: A HUD Section 8 program that pays the owners of specific rental buildings part of the rent of units let to low-income households, through a contract tied to the building rather than to the tenant (unlike a housing choice voucher).
eCFR, 24 CFR 880.101 Section 8 housing assistance payments program, applicability
proportional-symbol-map: A map in which each place has a circle whose area is proportional to its value. It suits counts, such as jobs.
Esri ArcGIS Pro documentation, Proportional symbology
provider-taxonomy: The national code list of health care provider types and specialties (for example 207Q00000X, family medicine). Each provider picks one primary code in the NPI registry.
National Uniform Claim Committee, Health Care Provider Taxonomy
provisional-data: Values that the agency publishing them has not yet reviewed and approved, so they may still change. USGS marks its recent water readings provisional until its review is complete; then they are marked approved.
USGS Water Data API, daily values: Approval Status (Provisional or Approved; provisional data are subject to revision)
proxy: A measure used in place of one that cannot be observed directly, because the two are expected to move together. For example, Census seasonal-use vacant units are the public proxy for second homes and short-term rentals.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Seasonal, recreational or occasional-use units (number)
prtc: The Puerto Rico government tourism agency. It groups the 78 municipalities into seven tourism regions.
Puerto Rico Tourism Company, tourism regions
public-assistance-fema: FEMA money for repairing public facilities, such as roads, schools, power and water systems, after a disaster. The observatory shows the federal share obligated by municipality.
public-domain: Works free of copyright, which anyone may use without permission. Works of the US federal government are in the public domain in the United States; CC0 1.0 is a tool by which an owner dedicates a work to it.
public-housing: Rental housing owned and run by a public housing agency with HUD funds for eligible low-income families, elderly people and people with disabilities (residenciales públicos in Puerto Rico).
pupil-teacher-ratio: The number of pupils enrolled in a level of education divided by the number of teachers at that level. The pupil-qualified teacher ratio (SDG 4.c.4) counts only teachers with the minimum qualifications required, so it is higher than or equal to the plain ratio.
UNESCO Institute for Statistics, Glossary (UIS Data Browser)
purchasing-power: What a dollar buys compared with what it bought in another month: the base-period price index divided by the current one. When prices rise 25%, a dollar buys 80 cents of what it bought before.
Departamento del Trabajo y Recursos Humanos de Puerto Rico, Poder adquisitivo del dólar del consumidor
put: Plan de Uso de Terrenos (Land Use Plan)
The Junta de Planificación's plan that classes all land in Puerto Rico, for example as urban, urbanizable, ordinary rural or specially protected rural. The observatory uses the 2015 version.
Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos
publico: Spanish for a shared taxi or van that runs a route. Some públicos routes are mapped in OpenStreetMap, but no agency publishes their timetables as GTFS.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Públicos and other routes mapped in OpenStreetMap
qcew: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
A Bureau of Labor Statistics count of jobs and wages at employers covered by unemployment insurance, by where the employer's work site is.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
qgis: A free, open-source geographic information system for a desktop computer. It opens the observatory's files (GeoJSON, CSV), joins tables to them and makes maps and analyses.
qualified-low-income-community-investmen: A loan to, or an equity investment in, a business or project in a low-income community that a Community Development Entity makes with New Markets Tax Credit money. The CDFI Fund publishes each one with its census tract, year and amount.
26 U.S.C. 45D(d), Qualified low-income community investments (Cornell LII)
qualified-opportunity-fund: A corporation or partnership set up to invest in Opportunity Zones that holds at least 90% of its assets in property, stock or partnership interests there; investing a capital gain through one is what earns the zones' tax benefits (26 U.S.C. 1400Z-2(d)). A rural fund (QROF) holds them in zones made entirely of rural area.
26 U.S.C. 1400Z-2, Special rules for capital gains invested in opportunity zones (Cornell LII)
quantile: A cut point that splits the sorted values into groups of equal size (equal counts). Quintiles, terciles and percentiles are quantiles.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Percentiles
questioned-costs: Costs an auditor questions because they may break a rule of the federal award, lack documents to support them, or seem unreasonable. The federal agency decides later whether they must be paid back.
Code of Federal Regulations, 2 CFR 200.1 (definitions) and 200.516 (audit findings)
quintile: One of five groups holding the same number of values (a fifth of the sorted data each); the four cut points are the 20th, 40th, 60th and 80th percentiles. The map shades the municipalities in five equal-count classes by default.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Percentiles
radiance: The power of light that leaves a surface in one direction, per unit of area and per unit of solid angle (watts per square metre per steradian), as a satellite sensor measures it from above the atmosphere. Night-time lights give it in nanowatts per square centimetre per steradian (nW/cm²/sr): a higher value means a brighter place, not more lamps or more people.
NASA, VIIRS Black Marble Product User Guide, version 2.0 (October 2024)
rank: A municipality's position when the values are sorted from highest to lowest. Rank 1 is the highest value, not necessarily the best result.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Rank (1 = highest)
raster-data: Map data stored as a grid of equal cells, like a photo. Each cell holds one value for the piece of ground it covers, such as its temperature or its height. Zoomed in far enough, the cells show as squares.
QGIS Documentation, A Gentle Introduction to GIS: Raster Data
raster-tile: A square image of a map at one zoom level (usually 256 × 256 pixels, PNG or JPEG), drawn in advance by a server; the browser places the images side by side. The 2D map used raster tiles until 2026-10-23; the sea level rise layer and the USGS base maps (aerial imagery, topographic, shaded relief) still do.
rate: A number measured against a base, such as a percent or a count per 1,000 residents. The poverty rate is the share of people below the poverty level.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Per 1,000 residents
ratio: One number divided by another. The jobs per employed resident figure and the affordability ratio are ratios.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Share of the Puerto Rico total
real-time-data: Live information on where vehicles are now. The observatory has none for buses. Its 'vehicles now' view shows where vehicles should be on the timetable.
record: An observation unit of a data file: a feature of a GeoJSON file, a row of a table or, in a series file, an area in a period (a municipio in a year) that holds at least one value. The Data management page counts the records of every published data file.
PR Data Observatory, Data management: Definitions (Record)
recorded-as-statewide: Money that the source ties to Puerto Rico as a whole and not to a municipality. It is in the Puerto Rico total but in no municipality's figure. FEMA Public Assistance and federal awards both have such amounts.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: How federal award dollars are placed in a municipality
region: A tourism region: one of the seven groups into which the Puerto Rico Tourism Company sorts the municipalities. It is not a Census, planning or political unit.
Puerto Rico Tourism Company, tourism regions
regulatory-quality: A WGI dimension: perceptions of the government's ability to formulate and implement sound policies and regulations that permit and promote private-sector development. A standardized estimate centred on 0.
World Bank, Worldwide Governance Indicators: documentation (2026 update)
renewable-portfolio-standard: A law that requires a utility to get a growing share of its electricity from renewable sources by set dates. Puerto Rico's, in Act 17-2019, set 40% by 2025, 60% by 2040 and 100% by 2050; Act 1-2025 removed the 2025 and 2040 targets and kept 100% by 2050.
repeated-finding: An audit finding that the auditor marks as also reported in the audit before. It means the problem was still there a year later.
Code of Federal Regulations, 2 CFR 200.1 (definitions) and 200.516 (audit findings)
repository: The store of a project's files together with the full history of every change to them, kept with the version-control system Git. The observatory's repository on GitHub holds its code, build scripts and published data; a change reaches the site only once it is merged into the repository's main branch.
rescaling: Changing a number into a comparable form, such as per 1,000 residents or as a share. It is also called normalisation. The 'Show as' menu offers it.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: The 'Show as' menu: ways to rescale a dataset
residence-basis: Counting a person at the place where they live, wherever they work. Income, poverty and employed residents are on this basis.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Workplace basis and residence basis
residual: The difference between a place's observed value and the value the fitted line predicts. A standardised residual divides it by the standard deviation of the residuals.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Residuals
residual-method-migration: Estimating migration as what is left after deaths: the people counted at the end, minus the survivors of those counted at the start. Errors in either count end up in the estimate.
United Nations, Manual VI: Methods of Measuring Internal Migration (1970), chapter on the survival ratio method
river-flow-discharge: The volume of water that passes one point of a river each second. The observatory gives it in cubic metres per second (m³/s): one cubic metre is 1,000 litres. USGS calls it discharge or streamflow and measures it in cubic feet per second.
USGS, Water Science School: How streamflow is measured
rmp: A Risk Management Plan facility: a site that holds more than a threshold amount of certain hazardous chemicals and must file an accident-prevention and emergency plan with EPA under the Clean Air Act.
US EPA, Risk Management Program (RMP) rule
root-mean-square-error: The square root of the average squared error of a set of forecasts, in the units of the forecast. Large misses weigh more than small ones. For errors centred on zero and roughly normal, about 80% fall within 1.28 times it.
Hyndman, R. J. and Athanasopoulos, G., Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition (OTexts), section 5.8, Evaluating point forecast accuracy
roundabout: A circular intersection where traffic moves one way around a central island and entering vehicles yield to those already in the circle. OpenStreetMap tags it junction=roundabout; the observatory adds round road rings it draws without the tag.
rtap: A federal program whose online portal lists public transit timetable feeds. The observatory looks there for the GTFS feeds of municipal transit systems.
rule-of-law: A WGI dimension: perceptions of the extent to which people have confidence in and abide by the rules of society, in particular contract enforcement, property rights, the police and the courts, and the likelihood of crime and violence. A standardized estimate centred on 0.
World Bank, Worldwide Governance Indicators: documentation (2026 update)
running-slope: How steeply a path rises or falls in the direction you walk, as the rise over the distance: 1 in 12 (8.33%) means 1 m up for every 12 m along. Under the 2010 ADA Standards a ramp may be no steeper than 1 in 12.
US Access Board, 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, 405.2
rural-opportunity-zone: An Opportunity Zone made entirely of rural area: outside every city or town of more than 50,000 inhabitants and the urbanized areas joined to it (in Puerto Rico, Treasury took census designated places of more than 50,000 as the cities). Investments there through a rural fund get a 30% basis increase after five years instead of 10%.
US Treasury, Office of Tax Analysis: Methodology for determining eligible tracts comprised entirely of a rural area (March 2026)
rvi: The Risk and Vulnerability Indicators that Hunter College built for the WCRP program: each input becomes a percentile among barrios, the percentiles are added within six areas and ranked again, and the overall index is cut into quintiles (levels 1 to 5). A level compares barrios with each other; it is not an absolute measure of risk.
saffir-simpson-scale: The 1 to 5 scale of hurricane strength by wind speed. The observatory records the category a storm reached near Puerto Rico.
NOAA National Hurricane Center, Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale
saidi: The average number of minutes each customer of a utility is without power in a period: the minutes customers are out, added up, divided by the customers served (IEEE 1366). SAIFI is the average number of interruptions per customer. A figure 'without major event days' leaves out the days of storms and other extreme events.
US Energy Information Administration, Electric power sales, revenue, and energy efficiency Form EIA-861 detailed data files (reliability)
samhsa: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration

The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration of the US Department of Health and Human Services. Its national directories (N-SUMHSS) list substance use and mental health treatment facilities, which the observatory counts but does not draw.
sampling-error: The gap between a survey estimate and the true value that arises because only a sample of households was asked. The margin of error describes it. It does not cover mistakes in people's answers.
US Census Bureau, Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data (2020), chapter 7: Understanding error and determining statistical significance
scatter-plot: A chart with one dot per municipality: one dataset runs left to right and another bottom to top. The workbench draws one with a fitted line.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Scatter plot
scheduled-speed: The average speed a timetable plans for a trip: the distance from the first to the last timed stop divided by the scheduled time between them, in km/h, stops and waits included. It is the plan, not the speed observed on the street.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Scheduled speed
scheduled-stop: A stop that appears in a public timetable feed (GTFS). Stops that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap are not scheduled stops.
school-life-expectancy: The total number of years of schooling, from primary to tertiary, that a child of school-entrance age can expect to receive if current age-specific enrolment rates persist; the sum of those rates.
UNESCO Institute for Statistics, Glossary (UIS Data Browser)
scour-critical: A bridge whose foundations a flood could undermine: fast water can wash away the soil around its piers or abutments. FHWA codes it in item 113 of the National Bridge Inventory; codes 0 to 3 mean scour critical.
FHWA, Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (item 113)
seasonal-recreational-or-occasional-use-: A vacant housing unit held for part-year use, such as a weekend home. It is the closest public proxy for second homes and short-term rentals.
section-406-mitigation: Cost-effective work, paid as part of a FEMA Public Assistance repair, that protects a damaged public facility from future damage beyond restoring it to its pre-disaster design (Stafford Act section 406; 44 CFR 206.226(e)).
eCFR, 44 CFR 206.226 Restoration of damaged facilities, paragraph (e) Hazard mitigation
self-employed: Working for oneself in one's own business. The share of self-employed residents is a rough indicator of work that the jobs data do not fully cover, and it mixes formal and informal work.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Glossary
sentinel-2: The European Union's Copernicus Earth-observing satellites (two at first, three today), run by the European Space Agency since 2015. Their camera sees 13 bands of light, four of them at 10 m, including the red and near-infrared used for NDVI; together they view each place every 2 to 5 days, in the late morning (10:30 local solar time).
service-gap: A census block with 40 or more residents whose nearest scheduled stop is more than 800 m away.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Residents far from service (service-gap rule)
sfha: Special Flood Hazard Area: the area that FEMA maps as having a 1% chance of flooding in any year (in Puerto Rico's maps, zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99, V and VE). The observatory flags tourism places whose point falls inside it.
FEMA, Glossary: Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA)
shaded-relief: A picture of the shape of the ground computed from elevation data: each slope is shaded as if lit from one or more directions, so hills, ridges and valleys stand out. It shows shape, not height values. The USGS shaded relief base map is made from 3DEP elevation data, lit from several directions.
USGS, The National Map: USGS Shaded Relief base map service (service description)
share: A part as a percent of a whole, for example a municipality's jobs as a percent of Puerto Rico's jobs.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Share of the Puerto Rico total
shoreline-clipped-boundary: A boundary cut at the coast so that it shows land only. The legal municipal boundaries run about three nautical miles out to sea.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Shoreline-clipped boundaries versus 2020 legal boundaries
signalised-junction: An intersection controlled by traffic signals (red, yellow and green lights), as the MUTCD defines them. OpenStreetMap marks each signal as a node; the observatory joins nodes closer than 40 m into one junction.
FHWA, Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD), Part 4: Highway Traffic Signals
simplified-geometry: A shape with fewer points, so it loads faster. The map draws simplified copies, while the build's calculations use the full-detail shapes.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Simplified display geometry
simulated-connection: A line the observatory draws between two municipios where 500 or more workers travel between them and no timetabled transit route joins them. It follows the fastest roads between the two town centres. It shows where a connection is missing; it is not a proposed route.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Simulated connections between municipios
single-audit: A yearly audit that a state or local government, tribe, college or nonprofit must have when it spends $750,000 or more of federal awards in its fiscal year ($1,000,000 for fiscal years that start on or after 1 October 2024). It covers the entity's financial statements and its federal programs together, and it is filed with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse.
skewness: A measure of the lack of symmetry of a distribution: zero for a symmetric one, positive when the right tail is longer. The GII treats an indicator whose absolute skewness exceeds 2.25 (and kurtosis 3.5) as having outliers.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Measures of skewness and kurtosis
slope-percent: How steep the ground is: the rise over the horizontal run, times 100. A 10% slope climbs 10 m in 100 m; 100% is 45 degrees. Computed for each cell of an elevation model from the heights around it.
QGIS User Guide, Raster terrain analysis: Slope
slosh-mom: Sea, Lake and Overland Surges from Hurricanes, Maximum of MEOWs (Maximum Envelopes of Water)
NOAA's storm surge model (SLOSH) run for thousands of hypothetical hurricanes. A MOM map keeps, for each place, the highest water of all the storms of one category: a near worst case, not one storm.
NOAA National Hurricane Center, Sea, Lake, and Overland Surges from Hurricanes (SLOSH)
slr: A rise in the average level of the sea. The observatory shows NOAA's scenarios of 1 to 10 feet as a what-if layer, not as a forecast for a year.
NOAA Office for Coastal Management, Sea Level Rise Viewer
smart-meter-ami: An electric meter that records use at short intervals and sends the readings to the utility, so bills are read rather than estimated and outages are detected sooner. LUMA reports the share of customers with one in each municipio.
snapshot: A complete, dated build of the observatory's data, named by a label such as 'Snapshot 2026-10'. Every figure belongs to one snapshot; cite the label with it.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Snapshot labels and rebuilds
social-capital-wcrp: The community assets that a place can draw on, such as community centres, libraries, parks and organizations. The WCRP Social Capital map counts them for each Comunidad Especial and per resident by municipio.
social-security-disability-benefits: Monthly Social Security payments to insured workers who have a disability that keeps them from working, before they reach full retirement age, and to some of their family members. Also called Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI).
eCFR, 20 CFR 404.315 Who is entitled to disability benefits?
spatial-interpolation: Estimating a value at a place where nothing was measured from the values measured at points around it. The fewer the points and the farther apart they are, the less the estimate can be trusted.
QGIS Documentation, A Gentle Introduction to GIS: Spatial Analysis (Interpolation)
spatial-join: Giving each shape of one layer the facts of the shape of another layer that it falls in or touches: each point gets the name of the barrio around it. Counting points by area is a spatial join followed by a count.
QGIS User Guide, Vector general: Join attributes by location
spearman-rank-correlation: Pearson's r computed on the ranks of the values instead of the values themselves, from −1 to +1: it measures how monotonic the relationship is (whether one rises when the other rises, in a straight line or not) and is less affected by outliers. The workbench's Correlations view offers it as "Spearman (rank order)", and the WCRP page uses it to compare the order of the barrios in two versions of the index.
NIST Dataplot reference manual, RANK CORRELATION
srep: Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido (specially protected rural land)
Rural land that the land use plan keeps out of urban development because of a special value or risk, such as ecology, farmland, water or scenery.
Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos
standard-deviation: A measure of spread: the square root of the mean squared deviation from the mean, σ = √(Σ(x − x̄)² / n). The observatory uses this population formula (dividing by n, the number of municipalities) for its z-scores; for a normal distribution about 68% of the values lie within one standard deviation of the mean.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Measures of scale
standby-generator: A generator that is available for service but not normally used, in EIA's status codes (SB, standby or backup). Many run only when other units fail or demand peaks, or, at factories and hospitals, when the grid goes down. EIA counts them with the operating generators.
US Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-860M (Monthly Update to the Annual Electric Generator Report)
statistically-significant: Large enough that it is unlikely to be only the chance variation of a survey. The Census Bureau's rule compares a difference between two estimates with the margins of error of both.
US Census Bureau, Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data (2020), chapter 7: Understanding error and determining statistical significance
storm-surge: The rise of the sea that a hurricane's winds and low pressure push onto the land, above the normal tide. The observatory counts who lives where NOAA's SLOSH model shows it reaching in a near worst case for each hurricane category.
NOAA National Hurricane Center, Storm Surge Overview
str: A home or room rented for short stays. The observatory has no count of short-term rentals; the Census Bureau's seasonal-use vacant units are the closest public proxy.
Foundation for Puerto Rico, The State of Housing in Puerto Rico (2023)
straight-line-distance: The Euclidean distance between two points (as the crow flies), not along streets. The 400 m straight-line measures use it.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: The 400 m walking rule
sub-pillar-gii: A group of two to five indicators inside a pillar of the Global Innovation Index (21 in the GII 2020, such as 1.1 Political environment). Its score is the weighted average of its indicators' 0-100 scores.
Cornell University, INSEAD and WIPO, The Global Innovation Index 2020, Appendix III: Sources and definitions
subapplication-fema-grants: A request for one project or plan that a local government or other subapplicant submits through the recipient (in Puerto Rico, the Commonwealth) under a FEMA grant. Once approved and awarded it becomes a subaward, or subgrant.
FEMA, OpenFEMA data set HMA Subapplications - v2
subaward: An award that the prime recipient of a federal grant (the pass-through entity) makes to another organization, the subrecipient, to carry out part of the grant's work. It is part of the prime grant, not money added to it.
subrecipient: An organization that receives a subaward from the prime recipient of a federal grant (the pass-through entity) to carry out part of the grant's work, such as a municipio that runs part of a disaster recovery program. It answers to the pass-through entity, which answers to the federal agency.
substation: A facility of the grid where transformers change the voltage of electricity (for example from 115 kV to 13.2 kV) and switches connect or isolate lines. The observatory counts the substations mapped in OpenStreetMap by municipio and does not draw them.
suelo-rustico-comun: Spanish for ordinary rural land: rural land that the land use plan does not set aside for urban growth and does not specially protect.
Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos
suelo-urbanizable: Spanish for urbanizable land: land that is not built up yet but that the land use plan marks as able to become urban. Programado (programmed) land comes sooner and no programado (not programmed) land later.
Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos
suelo-urbano: Spanish for urban land: land that the land use plan classes as already built up for towns and cities, or set aside for urban use.
Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos
suppression: Also called disclosure suppression: withholding a figure so that it cannot reveal one employer. A blank in the jobs data means withheld, or no employer listed, never zero.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, QCEW overview
svi: An index by CDC and ATSDR of how hard a disaster may hit a community's people. It ranks each area on 16 survey measures in four themes (socioeconomic status, household characteristics, racial and ethnic minority status, housing type and transportation) and gives a percentile rank from 0, the least vulnerable, to 1, the most. Puerto Rico is ranked apart from the states.
tercile: One of three groups of the same size. A bivariate map cuts each dataset into three classes. When a layer uses quantile classes (the default), the cut points are terciles, and with 'Same classes in every year' on they are terciles of all years pooled, so one year can have unequal groups.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Percentiles
terrain-tile: A map tile that stores the ground's elevation instead of a picture, encoded in the colours of its pixels; the 3D view reads it to raise the ground. The observatory uses the open Terrain Tiles first published by Mapzen and hosted by Amazon Web Services.
Registry of Open Data on AWS, Terrain Tiles
tiger-and-tigerweb: Topologically Integrated Geographic Encoding and Referencing
The Census Bureau's mapping database and the web service that serves it. The observatory gets municipality and barrio boundaries and the population of census blocks from it.
US Census Bureau, TIGER data products guide
tile-provider: A service that cuts map data into tiles and serves them, with styles, fonts and icons, to web maps. It is separate from the data source: the observatory's main tile provider is OpenFreeMap, and its data source is OpenStreetMap. The USGS National Map is the provider, and the source, of the aerial imagery, topographic and shaded relief base maps.
time-series: Values of the same measure for a run of years.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Trend line in the inspector and the Trend chart
timepoint: A stop whose time in the timetable is exact; times at other stops are approximate or left out (GTFS stop_times.txt, field timepoint). A timetable with only two timepoints per trip (timetable only) gives no time between its first and last stop.
timetable: A published schedule of the times at which vehicles serve each stop on each trip. The observatory reads timetables in GTFS format; "schedule-based" figures come from them, not from vehicles observed.
topographic-map: A reference map that shows the shape and height of the land, with contour lines and shaded relief, together with water, land cover, roads, boundaries and place names. The USGS Topo base map draws these from the public-domain data of the USGS National Map, at every scale from the world to a street.
USGS, The National Map: USGS Topo base map service (service description)
topology: How shapes on a map relate to each other: which areas share an edge, which area holds a point, whether areas leave gaps or overlap. A layer with clean topology has no gaps or overlaps where its areas meet.
QGIS, A Gentle Introduction to GIS, Topology
tourism-place: A listing of an attraction, restaurant or bar, lodging or visitor service from Overture Maps, sorted by FPR into four categories. It is a listing, not a count of businesses or visits.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Which places the observatory counts (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship)
transfer: Changing from one transit route to another to finish a trip. A trip with a transfer takes longer and depends on the two timetables meeting.
transmission-line: A high-voltage line that carries electricity in bulk from power plants to substations, over long distances; distribution lines then carry it at lower voltage along the streets to homes and businesses. In Puerto Rico the transmission voltages are 230 and 115 kV, and 38 kV is the subtransmission network.
travel-time-area-isochrone: The area that can be reached from a point within a given time, along a network such as the roads, at a set speed. A 15-minute walk along winding streets covers far less than a circle of the same distance.
QGIS User Guide, Network analysis: Service area (from point)
tree-cover-loss: A 30 m pixel where trees taller than 5 m were removed or killed (a stand-replacing disturbance) in a given year, from the Hansen Global Forest Change maps. Hurricane damage, fire and clearing all count, even where the trees grow back, so it is not the same as deforestation.
University of Maryland, Hansen Global Forest Change 2000-2024 (v1.12)
tren-urbano: The rail line of the San Juan area. Its stations and timetable are in the ATI feed.
tri: The Toxics Release Inventory: an EPA database in which industrial facilities report each year how much of listed toxic chemicals they release or manage. The observatory counts the reporting facilities by barrio.
US EPA, What is the Toxics Release Inventory?
type-i-crimes: The eight Type I offences in the Puerto Rico Police's municipal tables, following the FBI's Uniform Crime Reporting model: murder, rape, human trafficking, robbery and aggravated assault (violent), and burglary, larceny and vehicle theft (property). The counts are complaints recorded (querellas), not every crime that happened.
Policía de Puerto Rico, Delitos Tipo I, informe de diciembre de 2022, tabla por municipio (Instituto de Estadísticas de Puerto Rico)
uis: The UNESCO Institute for Statistics, the United Nations' statistical office for education, science, culture and communication; it publishes the education and R&D series of most economies, Puerto Rico included, through its data browser and API.
unemployment-rate: The share of the labor force that is looking for work and has none. The BLS series is a model estimate; the survey series comes from the American Community Survey.
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Glossary
urban-heat-island: An urban area that is hotter than the land around it, because its pavement, roofs and buildings absorb and hold the sun's heat, it has fewer trees and plants, and its activities release heat. EPA distinguishes surface heat islands (the ground and roofs, strongest by day) from atmospheric heat islands (the air, often strongest at night).
U.S. EPA, Learn About Heat Islands
usac: The Universal Service Administrative Company, the nonprofit that administers the federal Universal Service Fund programs, including E-Rate, for the Federal Communications Commission.
usaspending: The US government's public website for federal awards. The observatory uses awards by place of performance, by federal fiscal year.
usgs: A US science agency. It publishes the Protected Areas Database (PAD-US).
utc: The world's time standard. Puerto Rico keeps Atlantic Standard Time all year, four hours behind UTC. The observatory gives build times in UTC.
NIST, How UTC(NIST) is related to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)
utci: A thermal comfort index in °C: the air temperature of a reference environment that would cause the same physiological response in a model person as the actual conditions of air temperature, humidity, wind and radiation. Its scale runs from extreme cold stress to extreme heat stress; 32 to 38 °C is strong heat stress, 38 to 46 °C very strong and above 46 °C extreme.
UTCI, Universal Thermal Climate Index (ISB Commission 6)
v-zone: The part of FEMA's Special Flood Hazard Area along the coast where waves of 3 feet or more are expected in the 1% annual chance flood, besides the flooding itself (zones V and VE).
vacancy-rate: Vacant housing units as a share of all housing units. Vacant units include homes for sale or rent, seasonal homes and abandoned units.
value-data-point: A non-null observation: one field of one record that holds a number, a code or a text; a list cell counts its elements. Null, absent and empty values, metadata, geometry coordinates and lookup tables are not values.
PR Data Observatory, Data management: Definitions (Value (data point))
ve-zone: A FEMA coastal high hazard area: part of the Special Flood Hazard Area (1% annual chance) where waves of 3 feet or more add to the flood. V zones have no base flood elevation; VE zones have one.
vector-data: Map data drawn as points, lines and areas. Each shape is stored as the coordinates of its corners and carries facts about the thing it stands for. A vector shape stays sharp however far you zoom in.
QGIS Documentation, A Gentle Introduction to GIS: Vector Data
vector-tile: A square piece of a map at one zoom level that holds the map's features as geometry (points, lines, polygons) with attributes, not as a picture; the browser draws it with a style, so labels stay sharp and colours can change without new downloads.
vehicle-kilometre: One vehicle driving one kilometre. Adding them up over a road network measures how much driving happens on it: 1,000 cars each driving 10 km make 10,000 vehicle-km.
FHWA, Highway Statistics: vehicle-miles of travel
vertex: A position of a geometry (a longitude and latitude pair, RFC 7946) in a polygon, a line or a point, including the closing position of each ring. The Data management page reports vertices apart from values.
PR Data Observatory, Data management: Definitions (Vertex)
veterans-disability-compensation: A monthly, tax-free payment from the US Department of Veterans Affairs to veterans with a disability caused or made worse by their military service.
vintage: One year's release of Census Bureau estimates. A later vintage can revise earlier years. In the 2026-10 snapshot the observatory uses Vintage 2020 and Vintage 2025 for population.
US Census Bureau, Population estimates glossary
vnp46a3: VIIRS/NPP Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Monthly L3 Global 15 arc second Linear Lat Lon Grid

NASA's monthly Black Marble product of night-time lights, from the Day/Night Band of the VIIRS instrument on the Suomi NPP satellite, January 2012 on: each 15 arc-second pixel (about 460 m at Puerto Rico's latitude) holds the month's radiance composite of clear nights, corrected for moonlight, with the number of observations and a quality flag. The observatory reads collection 2 (DOI 10.5067/VIIRS/VNP46A3.002).
NASA LAADS DAAC, VNP46A3 product page
walking-distance-along-mapped-roads: The length of the shortest path between two points along the roads mapped in OpenStreetMap. It leaves out footpaths, sidewalks, steps and crossings that are not mapped, so it is an estimate, and it is always at least the straight-line distance.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: The 400 m walking rule
wastewater-treatment-plant-potw: A plant that treats the sewage of a town before it is discharged to a river or the sea. In EPA's records a publicly owned one is a POTW (publicly owned treatment works); in Puerto Rico most are run by the Aqueduct and Sewer Authority (AAA).
EPA, National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System: Municipal Wastewater
water-surface-elevation: The height of a lake's or reservoir's water above a reference level, here local mean sea level, in metres. A reservoir's level falls in a drought and rises after rain; it is not the volume of water, because sediment fills part of a reservoir over time.
USGS, Water Data for the Nation: parameter 72376, lake or reservoir elevation above local mean sea level
watershed-huc: The land whose rain drains to one river, lake or bay. The USGS numbers watersheds in nested levels: 2 digits for a region, 8 for a subbasin (HUC-8), 12 for a subwatershed (HUC-12) of roughly 40 to 160 km² in Puerto Rico.
wcrp: WCRP helps communities in Puerto Rico design their own resilience plans (their vision, needs and goals). Foundation for Puerto Rico runs it in collaboration with PRDOH, with CDBG-DR funds from HUD. The observatory maps the program's communities, with the state of each plan, and the Risk and Vulnerability Indicators by barrio.
webgl: A browser programming interface, based on OpenGL ES, that draws 2D and 3D graphics with the device's graphics processor. MapLibre needs it to draw the vector base map and the 3D view; with WebGL off, the 2D maps show their data without a base map.
MDN Web Docs, WebGL: 2D and 3D graphics for the web
weekday-calls-departures: How many times, on a typical weekday (a Wednesday), the published timetable has a vehicle call at a stop. The map calls them weekday departures. It is not a wait time: it adds up all routes and every direction, and at a terminal it includes vehicles that arrive and end their run.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Scheduled weekday calls at the stop (shown on the map as weekday departures)
wgi: The World Bank's six aggregate governance indicators for more than 200 economies since 1996, each built with an unobserved components model from dozens of surveys and expert assessments and reported as a standardized estimate (mean 0, standard deviation 1, mostly between -2.5 and 2.5) with a standard error. Each release revises all past years.
World Bank, Worldwide Governance Indicators: documentation (2026 update)
wgs-84: The reference system that GPS and web maps use to give latitude and longitude. The observatory's coordinates for places and stops are in WGS 84.
winsorization: Treatment of outliers that replaces the most extreme values of a distribution by the next value inside it, without dropping any observation. In the GII an indicator with one to five outliers is winsorized until its skewness and kurtosis fall within the set thresholds; the capped economies then tie at the top or the bottom of the 0-100 scale.
WIPO, Global Innovation Index 2026, Appendix I: Conceptual and measurement framework
workbench: The panel that the Workbench button opens from Tools › Analysis. Its views work on the visible layers: Inspector, Table, Scatter, Trend, Correlations, Small multiples, Compare two maps, Composite, Scenarios and Study areas.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Workbench: Correlations tab (correlation matrix)
workplace-basis: Counting a job at the place where the work is done, not where the worker lives. Jobs and wages in the observatory are on this basis.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Workplace basis and residence basis
year-bar: The control that sets the year for every dataset on the map and the Housing page. 'Latest' shows each dataset's own last year.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Nearest-year rule (latest value at or before the chosen year)
year-chip: The small note beside each layer that says which year of data it shows, for example '2019 (latest at or before 2020)', 'first data 2014' or 'snapshot 2026'.
PR Data Observatory, data dictionary: Nearest-year rule (latest value at or before the chosen year)
zonal-statistics: A summary (mean, median, count or share) of the cells of a raster, such as a satellite image of surface temperature, that fall inside each zone of another layer: a barrio, a study area or a buffer. The result describes the zone as a whole, not any one place in it.
